title: Claude Certified Architect – Foundations: 390 practice questions
sourceType: Community practice questions, not an official Anthropic examination

questions.question: In a multi-agent research system, the web search subagent’s harness gets a response with stop_reason “max_tokens”. The last content block is a tool_use block whose input JSON stops partway through a field. What should the harness do next?

options.text: Treat the response as complete and pass the text generated so far to the coordinator as the final result.
Append a tool_result with is_error set to true for the truncated call and continue the loop.
Run the tool with the partial input after repairing the JSON by closing the unfinished braces.
Retry the request with a higher max_tokens value, then execute the complete tool call it returns.

questions.question: A research coordinator’s harness treats a run as finished when the assistant text contains “Research complete”, and it also treats reaching its 15-turn cap as a normal finish. Both checks misfire in production. How should the harness detect completion?

options.text: Check the final ResultMessage.stop_reason and treat the value “end_turn” as a completed run.
Read the stream through to its ResultMessage, treat subtype “success” as completion and handle “error_max_turns” as an incomplete run.
Tell the report subagent to end its final answer with a fixed marker token and stop the loop when that token appears.
Stop reading at the first assistant message that has no tool calls and treat it as the finished report.

questions.question: A research system must escalate a source conflict to a human analyst: a 2022 government report gives a 12% market share and a 2024 industry survey using a different method gives 31%. Analysts can’t see session transcripts and triage each case in a few minutes. How should the handoff be written?

options.text: A structured handoff with both figures mapped to their sources and publication dates, the checks already run, and a recommended next step.
A structured handoff that lists both figures with source names, labels them contradictory and asks the analyst to choose the more credible source.
A structured handoff that reports the 2024 figure as current, with its source and date, and marks the 2022 figure as superseded.
A structured handoff with both figures, sources and dates, plus the complete search and analysis subagent outputs as supporting evidence.

questions.question: A user asks three independent questions about one company: market position, recent litigation and financial health. The coordinator holds a background profile that all three investigations need. One search subagent currently answers all three, and coverage is shallow. How should the coordinator restructure the work?

options.text: Split the request into three subtasks, include the background profile in each prompt and emit the three Agent tool calls in one response.
Keep one subagent, give it the background profile and tell it to answer the three questions one after another.
Spawn three parallel subagents with short prompts naming each question, so they read the profile from the coordinator’s history.
Run three subagents in sequence, passing each one the profile plus the findings of the subagent that ran before it.

questions.question: Yesterday an engineer started a Claude Code session named citation-debug to find out why the synthesis subagent drops citations. This morning a short, unrelated session ran in the same directory. No repository files have changed. How should the engineer continue the investigation?

options.text: Start a new session and paste a structured summary of yesterday’s findings as the first message.
Run claude –resume citation-debug to reopen that named session with its context.
Run claude –continue to reopen the most recent conversation in the current directory.
Run claude -p with a prompt asking Claude to continue the citation-debug investigation.

questions.question: A teammate suggests letting the document analysis subagent send its findings straight to the synthesis subagent to save a turn. You need every finding to pass through the coordinator, with a guarantee that holds on unattended runs. Which two design choices achieve this? (select two)

options.text: Give both subagents a shared findings file that each one reads and writes during the task.
Add a rule to each subagent’s system prompt that results may be reported only to the coordinator.
Have the coordinator collect each subagent’s result and place the findings in the synthesis subagent’s prompt.
List each subagent’s tools explicitly in its AgentDefinition and leave SendMessage out of the list.

questions.question: A coordinator sends document analysis tasks to the built-in general-purpose subagent instead of the document analysis agent. That agent’s prompt field describes its tasks in detail, but its description field only says “Helps with documents.” What fixes the routing?

options.text: Expand the agent’s prompt field with more explicit examples of the document tasks it handles.
Rewrite the description field to state which document analysis tasks this agent handles.
Add the Agent tool to the document analysis agent’s tools list in its AgentDefinition.
Add few-shot delegation examples to the coordinator’s system prompt that route document tasks to this agent.

questions.question: A research coordinator receives a request on an emerging topic whose structure is unknown. The team’s fixed subtopic template missed key areas on similar topics before, and the token budget is limited. Which decomposition approach fits?

options.text: Spawn parallel subagents for every plausible subtopic at the start so no angle is missed, then synthesize all the outputs.
Reuse the fixed subtopic template from past reports and delegate each subtopic to the search and analysis subagents in parallel.
Delegate one broad research task per subagent and let the synthesis subagent request follow-up research for gaps it finds.
Run a short scoping pass that maps the topic’s structure, then build a prioritized delegation plan that adapts as findings arrive.

questions.question: Legal requires that a research system’s web search subagent never sends a request to a list of restricted domains. Prompt instructions failed in testing, and the subagent must keep fetching approved sources. Which design enforces the rule?

options.text: Add the restricted-domain list with explicit refusal instructions to the search subagent’s AgentDefinition system prompt.
Add a PreToolUse hook matching WebFetch that returns a deny decision when the requested URL is on the restricted list.
Add a PostToolUse hook matching WebFetch that removes restricted-domain content from the result before the model reads it.
Add WebFetch to the search subagent’s disallowedTools so it can’t send any outbound web request.

questions.question: A coordinator’s baseline session holds the full research history, and its final turns contain the consolidated citation list. The team needs two report-strategy branches that both include those final turns, and the baseline must stay unchanged. How should they create the branches?

options.text: Resume the baseline twice with fork_session enabled and resume_session_at set to the message where the last subagent returned.
Resume the baseline session ID twice with fork_session enabled, so each strategy gets its own new session.
Open two new sessions and give each a structured summary of the baseline’s conclusions as its first prompt.
Copy the baseline’s stored transcript to two new session IDs and resume each copy separately.

questions.question: A research coordinator uses dynamic adaptive decomposition for every request. A weekly competitor briefing must always have the same five sections, but some runs skip one. Open-ended deep-dive requests work well. What should change?

options.text: Convert both workflows to fixed pipelines so every run follows the same reproducible steps.
Add the five required sections to the coordinator’s system prompt as a checklist to follow when planning the briefing.
Keep dynamic decomposition for the briefing and add an evaluation loop that detects missing sections and re-delegates.
Run the briefing as a fixed pipeline with one step per section and keep dynamic decomposition for deep dives.

questions.question: A research system’s generate_report tool publishes finished reports straight to a client portal. Policy requires verify_citations to pass before any report is published. The system prompt states this order, but logs show the check is sometimes skipped. The pipeline runs unattended overnight with no one to approve actions. Which design guarantees compliance?

options.text: Move the ordering rule to the top of the coordinator’s system prompt and mark it IMPORTANT with numbered steps.
Add a PreToolUse hook that blocks any generate_report call until verify_citations has returned a passing result.
Add a PostToolUse hook on generate_report that runs the citation check on the output and reports failures to the coordinator.
Add a PreToolUse hook on generate_report that returns an ask decision, requiring approval before each publish.

questions.question: Your coordinator spawns all four extraction subagents for every document and copies the document into each prompt. Plain invoices need only field extraction, but new document types keep arriving, so the specialist combinations can’t be fixed in advance. Which two changes stop the unneeded delegations? (select two)

options.text: Add a routing step that classifies each document into fixed categories, each mapped to a preset list of subagents.
Tell every subagent to inspect the document when invoked and return ’not applicable’ if its specialty isn’t needed.
Prompt the coordinator to assess each document first and emit Agent tool calls only for the specialists that apply.
Write each subagent’s AgentDefinition description to state which document characteristics call for that specialist.

questions.question: In an extraction system, an extraction agent passes prose summaries of its findings to a report agent that can’t read the original files. Auditors find that values in final reports often lack their source document name and page number. What fixes this?

options.text: Add a prompt instruction telling the extraction agent to always mention sources in its summaries.
Have the extraction agent emit each value as a structured record with source document name and page number fields.
Have the report agent reopen each source document and find the page for every value before writing.
Append a list of all source document names to the end of each summary before the handoff.

questions.question: A paused named session holds a detailed analysis of several files in an inventory service. Teammates have since merged changes to a few of those files, and the merged code must stay. Which two approaches correctly continue the work? (select two)

options.text: Use file checkpointing to restore the analyzed files to the state the session last saw.
Start a new session and seed it with a structured summary of the earlier session’s conclusions.
Use fork_session to branch from the saved context and continue from the fork’s view of those files.
Resume the session and name the changed files so the agent re-reads them before continuing.

questions.question: A custom agent loop appends the assistant tool_use message, then a user message with a short status note required for the audit trail, then a second user message with the tool_result blocks. The API rejects the request with a 400 error, and the note must stay in the conversation history. What fixes the request?

options.text: Keep the message order and set is_error to true on each tool_result so Claude treats the turn as a failed tool execution.
Remove the status-note message so the tool_result message directly follows the assistant message.
Send the tool_result blocks in the user message right after the assistant message, and put the status note as text after them.
Combine the note and the tool_result blocks in one user message, with the note’s text block first.

questions.question: To protect credentials, a team added a PreToolUse hook that denies Read calls on any path under secrets/. When an engineer writes @secrets/db.env in a prompt, the file contents still load. What should the team change?

options.text: Add a CLAUDE.md rule telling Claude never to read files under secrets/.
Broaden the hook matcher so it also covers Grep and Glob calls on secrets/ paths.
Add a Read deny permission rule that covers the secrets/ path.
Add a PostToolUse hook that redacts secret values from Read results before Claude sees them.

questions.question: For one internal utility, a team calls the Messages API directly and writes its own tool loop for client-side tools that its code runs. Which two loop-control practices are correct? (select two)

options.text: Wait for the final ResultMessage and confirm its subtype is success before reading the result field.
Treat stop_reason “max_tokens” as a truncated response that needs handling, not as completion.
Treat stop_reason “pause_turn” as the signal that Claude is waiting for a client tool to run.
Keep looping while stop_reason is “tool_use”, running the requested tools and returning tool_result blocks.

questions.question: Engineers ask a developer-productivity agent open-ended questions such as “trace how a legacy config flag flows through the code,” where each tool result decides what to inspect next. A teammate wants a fixed tool order because logs vary between runs. Which control-flow design fits?

options.text: Replace the loop with a fixed pipeline that always runs Glob, then Grep, then Read.
Write numbered tool-use procedures into the system prompt so every investigation follows the same steps.
Add a classifier that detects the question type and runs a predetermined tool sequence for it.
Keep a model-driven loop in which Claude chooses each next tool based on earlier tool results.

questions.question: Stuck tasks escalate to on-call engineers who can’t see the agent’s session. An intake script parses each handoff for root cause, affected files and a recommended action, but prose handoffs sometimes leave these out. What design fixes this?

options.text: Constrain each escalation message to a JSON schema with required fields using structured outputs.
Attach the agent’s complete tool-call log and transcript to each escalation.
Route each prose handoff through a second Claude instance that checks it for completeness.
Add several few-shot examples of complete handoffs to the escalation section of the system prompt.

questions.question: A support agent’s policy allows autonomous refunds only within 30 days of delivery. Prompt instructions still let some late refunds through, and refunds post to the payment processor immediately and can’t be reversed. Which design guarantees compliance?

options.text: State the 30-day rule in the process_refund description and make delivery_date a required input field.
Add few-shot examples showing in-window refunds proceeding and late ones being escalated.
Add a PostToolUse hook on lookup_order that computes a refund_eligible flag and adds it to the result.
Add a PreToolUse hook that denies process_refund calls outside the window and redirects to escalate_to_human.

questions.question: An engineer’s shell profile exports CLAUDE_CODE_SKIP_PROMPT_HISTORY=1. Yesterday’s debugging session was named refund-triage, but today claude –resume refund-triage finds nothing and the picker is empty. How should the engineer make future sessions resumable by name?

options.text: Pass –resume the absolute path of the earlier session’s .jsonl transcript.
Resume using the earlier session’s full session ID instead of its name.
Unset CLAUDE_CODE_SKIP_PROMPT_HISTORY so session transcripts are saved to disk.
Run /rename refund-triage in a fresh session so the name is registered for resume.

questions.question: A support agent’s PostToolUse hook matches get_customer and lookup_order and converts their mixed timestamps to ISO 8601. Transcripts show Claude still reasons over the raw values, and the tools have no format parameters. What should the hook do?

options.text: Return hookSpecificOutput with updatedToolOutput set to the normalized result.
Exit with code 2 and write the normalized values to stderr so Claude receives them as feedback.
Print the normalized values to stdout and exit with code 0 to add them to the context.
Move the conversion to a PreToolUse hook that returns updatedInput requesting ISO 8601 output.

questions.question: A support agent gets subagents described only as “Handles billing questions” and “Handles order and return questions.” The coordinator now delegates even simple order-status checks, adding latency, and complex billing disputes usually include an order number too. Which change best stops the unnecessary delegation?

options.text: Include the coordinator’s already-fetched customer and order data in each subagent prompt so spawns finish faster.
Add a PreToolUse hook that denies subagent spawns whenever the message contains an order number.
Remove get_customer and lookup_order from the coordinator so all data access goes through subagents.
Rewrite each subagent’s description to name the complex cases it handles and mark single-lookup requests as out of scope.

questions.question: A support coordinator verifies the customer, confirms a duplicate charge with lookup_order, then spawns a refund-assessment subagent with “Assess whether this duplicate charge qualifies for a refund.” The subagent replies that no order was given. The design deliberately keeps raw backend output out of each specialist’s context. What should you change?

options.text: Define the subagent as a fork of the coordinator’s session so it inherits the history.
Have the coordinator restate the order details in its own assistant message just before spawning.
Include the customer ID, order ID and relevant charge details in the subagent’s prompt.
Tell the subagent in its AgentDefinition system prompt to call lookup_order before assessing.

questions.question: A long support session verified the customer and looked up two orders, then pursued a refund approach the team rejected. The team wants a branch that keeps those exact earlier tool results, drops the rejected turns and leaves the original session unchanged. How should they create it?

options.text: Start a new session whose first prompt summarizes the verification and order findings.
Resume the original session ID and continue from the latest turn with the new approach.
Resume with fork_session enabled to get a new session ID and a copy of the full history.
Resume with fork_session enabled and resume_session_at set to the UUID of the last message to keep.

questions.question: For a doc-lookup utility, a team calls the Messages API directly with the web search server tool. Its loop treats every stop_reason other than “tool_use” as completion. Long research prompts sometimes return “pause_turn”, and users then see unfinished summaries. How should the code handle a “pause_turn” response?

options.text: Treat it as a transient failure and retry the original request with exponential backoff.
Send the response’s assistant content back in a follow-up request so the server tool loop can continue.
Resend the request with a larger max_tokens value so the whole answer fits in one response.
Extract the tool_use block, run the web search in application code and return a tool_result.

questions.question: A developer-productivity agent maps a legacy module’s conventions over several turns, then spawns a code-generation subagent with “Generate adapters following the conventions identified above.” The subagent ignores them, and conventions differ per module. What should change?

options.text: Resume the subagent with the parent session’s ID so it continues from the earlier context.
Put the mapped conventions and file paths directly in the delegation prompt sent to the subagent.
Write the conventions into the shared project CLAUDE.md so subagents load them at startup.
Move the conventions into the subagent’s AgentDefinition system prompt so they load every time.

questions.question: An audit finds one refund ran before identity verification. An engineer proposes replacing the support agent loop with a hard-coded decision tree so the order can never be violated. Which two design choices are correct? (select two)

options.text: Replace the agent loop with a classifier that maps each request category to a fixed tool sequence.
Add a system prompt rule that process_refund must never run before get_customer, repeated every turn.
Add a programmatic precondition that blocks process_refund until get_customer has returned a verified customer ID.
Keep model-driven tool selection for investigation, where Claude picks the next tool from context.

questions.question: One customer message contains three concerns: a duplicate charge on order #4451, a refund whose amount depends on what the duplicate-charge check finds, and an unrelated shipping address change. How should the agent structure the investigation before replying?

options.text: Have the duplicate-charge subagent spawn the refund subagent itself when it finishes.
Spawn three parallel subagents in one turn, one per concern, each with the customer record.
Handle all three concerns in sequence inside the main agent without delegating.
Run the address-change and duplicate-charge subagents in parallel, then assess the refund once the duplicate-charge result is back.

questions.question: You register a PreToolUse hook with the matcher “process_refund”. Unit tests show its callback denies amounts above $500. The refund tool runs on an MCP server named “support”. In production the hook never fires and large refunds go through. What fixes this?

options.text: Register the hook on PostToolUse instead, because MCP tools trigger only that event.
Move the limit check into the MCP server, because SDK hooks don’t cover MCP tools.
Change the matcher to the tool’s full MCP name, mcp__support__process_refund.
Fix the callback’s comparison so it denies refunds above $500.

questions.question: A support agent requests get_customer and lookup_order in one turn. lookup_order times out, and one retry also fails. The agent must decide its next step now. How should the loop return the results to Claude?

options.text: Send one user message with the get_customer tool_result plus a lookup_order tool_result marked is_error true with the timeout details.
Send the get_customer result now and the lookup_order result in a later message after the next response.
Replace the missing lookup_order result with a plain text block describing the timeout.
Keep retrying lookup_order with backoff and send both results once the backend recovers.

questions.question: Engineers resume a named session daily to refine an agent’s MCP tool code. A few files change overnight, teammates forget to mention them, and Claude relies on stale results. What adds the recent changes to context automatically on every resume?

options.text: Start a fresh session each morning with a structured summary of the previous session.
Add a PostToolUse hook that appends each file’s last-modified time to every tool result.
Add a SessionStart hook that detects resumes and writes the list of files changed since the last session into context.
Add a CLAUDE.md instruction telling Claude to re-read every analyzed file at the start of each session.

questions.question: Internal project codenames must never appear in queries sent to the third-party MCP tool mcp__search__web_search, but the searches must still run. Prompt instructions still leaked codenames in testing. Which two steps enforce this? (select two)

options.text: Register a PostToolUse hook that deletes codenames from the search results.
In the hook callback, return a deny decision whenever the query contains a codename.
In the hook callback, read the query from tool_input and return updatedInput with the codename removed.
Register a PreToolUse hook whose matcher is mcp__search__web_search, the MCP tool naming pattern.

questions.question: An engineer is two hours into an unnamed session debugging a coordinator’s task decomposition. Short, unrelated sessions run in that directory every day. Tomorrow they want one command that reopens this exact investigation with full context and no session picker. What should they do?

options.text: Plan to run claude –continue tomorrow to reopen the most recent session in the directory.
Run claude –resume tomorrow without a session and pick the investigation from the list.
Run /rename with a descriptive name now, then resume it by that name tomorrow.
Exit and start a fresh session with claude -n to name it, then restart the investigation there.

questions.question: A research system’s PreToolUse hook exits with code 1 when the web search subagent’s fetch URL is on a licensing blocklist, yet logs show the blocked fetches still run. Research runs unattended overnight. What change enforces the rule?

options.text: Add the blocklist to the subagent’s system prompt with an instruction to refuse those domains.
Move the blocklist check to a PostToolUse hook that returns a blocking error.
Have the hook return JSON with permissionDecision “ask” for blocklisted URLs.
Have the hook exit with code 2 when the URL is on the blocklist.

questions.question: An earlier research investigation’s conclusions are still trusted, but most sources have since replaced their published figures, so the saved tool results must not re-enter context as evidence. The team starts a new coordinator session instead of resuming. What should its first prompt include?

options.text: The saved tool results, each labeled with its retrieval date and source.
Only the research topic and its list of subtopics.
The full search results and document analyses the earlier subagents returned.
The earlier conclusions and the claim-to-source mappings that support them.

questions.question: A research coordinator stores each subagent’s result separately but forwards all accumulated outputs to every downstream subagent. Report subagent prompts now reach 90K tokens, and the reports miss the synthesis conclusions. Every handoff must stay auditable in the coordinator’s logs. What should change?

options.text: Have the coordinator pass each subagent only the stored results its task needs.
Add a summarization subagent that condenses the accumulated outputs before they reach the report subagent.
Have the synthesis subagent send its output straight to the report subagent, bypassing the coordinator.
Move the report subagent to a model with a larger context window so everything fits.

questions.question: A custom code-explorer subagent (not the built-in Explore agent) mapped a legacy module and returned a brief summary with its agentId. A later spawn of the same agent type knows nothing about that work. Which two approaches give the follow-up access to the earlier context? (select two)

options.text: Spawn a fresh explorer from the same AgentDefinition so it keeps the first instance’s state.
Spawn a fresh explorer and point it at the earlier tool results in the coordinator’s history.
Ask Claude to resume the earlier explorer subagent by its agentId instead of spawning a new one.
Spawn the next explorer as a fork so it inherits the coordinator’s conversation history.

questions.question: A coordinator defines an explorer subagent through the SDK’s agents option with a detailed description, but the coordinator’s own tools list is limited to Read, Grep and Glob. At run time it never delegates and explores everything itself. What enables delegation?

options.text: Rewrite the explorer’s description to match exploration tasks more precisely.
Move the explorer definition into a .claude/agents/ Markdown file so it’s discovered at startup.
Set the coordinator’s permissionMode to dontAsk so spawn requests are approved automatically.
Add the Agent tool (formerly called Task) to the coordinator’s restricted tools list.

questions.question: A third-party MCP code-search tool returns more than 50 fields per result, and the agent needs only five. The server has no option to limit fields, and long exploration sessions run out of context. What should you implement?

options.text: A PreToolUse hook that returns updatedInput to rewrite each call so it asks for only five fields.
A trim_result tool that the agent is told to call on each raw result.
A system prompt instruction telling the agent to ignore all but the five fields.
A PostToolUse hook that strips the unused fields from each search result before the model processes it.

questions.question: A developer’s manual agent loop gets a single Grep tool_use block from Claude. The next request’s history holds the original user prompt, then a user message with exactly one tool_result whose tool_use_id copies Claude’s ID, with no text blocks. The API returns a 400 error for an unmatched tool_use_id. What fixes the request?

options.text: Generate a new unique tool_use_id for the tool_result instead of copying Claude’s.
Return an extra tool_result with is_error true for each tool_use the loop didn’t run.
Append Claude’s assistant message with its tool_use block to the history before the user message with the result.
Reorder the results message so every tool_result comes before any text block.

questions.question: A research coordinator’s delegation prompts give the web search subagent a fixed list of eight queries. On emerging topics, useful search terms only become clear after the first results, and the subagent returns thin findings. How should the delegation prompts change?

options.text: Rewrite the search subagent’s description to say it handles emerging, fast-moving topics.
Add extra query sets covering more categories of emerging topics in advance.
State the research goal and quality criteria, such as source count and cross-verification, and let the subagent choose its queries.
Keep the fixed queries, but have the coordinator re-delegate with a new list when findings are thin.

questions.question: Yesterday’s named session report-templates designed a citation format and edited three report templates. A teammate reverted the edits, so the exact diff is in git history, while the design reasoning exists only in that conversation. How should the engineer recover both?

options.text: Resume the session and have Claude rebuild the edits from its earlier tool results.
Start a new session and have Claude recover the decisions and edits from git history.
Restore the edits with git, then start a new session seeded with a written summary of the design.
Resume the session with claude –resume report-templates for the design context, and restore the edits through git.

questions.question: A report-generation stage always runs the same three steps: draft the report, check citations against the findings, then refine. Citation coverage must be confirmed before refinement runs. Which two design choices fit? (select two)

options.text: Reuse the research phase’s dynamic decomposition, letting the model pick each next step.
Implement the stage as a fixed prompt chain, with one call per step that processes the previous step’s output.
Add a programmatic gate after the citation check that blocks refinement until every claim maps to a finding.
Run the three steps as parallel calls and merge their outputs to cut latency.

questions.question: A team forks a baseline session into two branches to compare report structures. Branch A runs first and its report subagent edits reports/draft.md. When branch B runs, it reads that file and builds on A’s edits instead of the baseline draft. How should the branches be kept independent?

options.text: Fork each branch with resume_session_at set to a message before branch A wrote the draft.
Turn off session persistence for each branch so one branch’s state isn’t saved for the other.
Copy the baseline session’s entries to new keys in the session storage backend.
Run each forked branch in its own working directory with its own copy of the report files.

questions.question: A policy forbids force pushes to shared branches because rewritten history can’t be reliably restored. A PostToolUse hook with a Bash matcher detects force-push commands and returns a blocking response, but the pushes still reach the remote. Which change enforces the policy?

options.text: Extend the hook to run a compensating git command that restores the branch afterward.
Register the same check under PreToolUse so it runs before the Bash command executes.
Add a system prompt rule that the agent must never force-push to shared branches.
Change the hook’s return value to an explicit deny decision.

questions.question: Despite a system prompt rule against pushing to main, an agent’s unattended Bash runs pushed to main twice last month. Routine tests, builds and feature-branch pushes must keep running without approval. Which design enforces the rule?

options.text: A PreToolUse hook that inspects each Bash command and denies every git push.
The rule in CLAUDE.md with IMPORTANT emphasis and examples of allowed and forbidden commands.
A PostToolUse hook that inspects finished Bash commands and flags any push to main.
A PreToolUse hook that inspects each Bash command and denies any push to the main branch.

questions.question: A support agent’s escalation handoffs include the customer ID, an issue summary, the refund amount and a recommended action. Human agents triage each ticket in under two minutes and often re-offer resolutions the customer already declined. Which handoff change fixes this?

options.text: Attach the full session transcript to each ticket.
Have escalate_to_human attach the latest get_customer and lookup_order results.
Add an actions-taken section listing each resolution the agent tried and how the customer responded.
Have human agents start each case by asking the customer what was already tried.

questions.question: A pilot runs a support agent unattended in bypassPermissions mode so runs never stall on approval prompts. Pilot policy forbids autonomous refunds; every refund must go through escalate_to_human. Which two changes guarantee the agent can never execute process_refund? (select two)

options.text: Put a numbered rule at the top of the system prompt requiring refunds to go through escalate_to_human.
Remove process_refund from the agent’s allowedTools list.
Add process_refund to the agent’s disallowedTools configuration.
Add a permission deny rule that matches the process_refund tool.

questions.question: An engineer is starting a multi-day investigation into a drop in first-contact resolution, and other short sessions run in that directory every day. They want a scripted command that reopens the investigation directly each morning. Which setup works?

options.text: Start the session with claude -n escalation-spike, then run claude –resume escalation-spike each morning.
Start a normal session, then use fork_session each morning to branch from the previous day.
Start a normal session, then run claude –continue each morning.
Start a normal session, then run claude –resume each morning and pick it from the list.

questions.question: Policy now requires a supervisor to approve, in real time, any refund above $200 before it runs. Once approved, the refund must still complete in the same session, and smaller refunds should run without interruption. Which hook design meets this?

options.text: A PreToolUse hook on process_refund that denies amounts above $200.
A PreToolUse hook on process_refund that returns an ask decision for amounts above $200.
A PreToolUse hook that returns updatedInput capping refunds above $200 at $200.
A PostToolUse hook on process_refund that sends refunds above $200 to supervisor review.

questions.question: You add a fraud-check subagent whose description clearly covers chargeback requests, but the coordinator still skips it on about 1 in 10 chargebacks. Every chargeback needs a fraud check before the agent replies. Which change fixes this most reliably?

options.text: Redefine the subagent programmatically through the agents option so it takes precedence over filesystem agents.
Detect chargeback requests in your application and name the fraud-check subagent explicitly in the coordinator’s prompt.
Move the fraud-check subagent to the first position in the agents configuration.
Expand its description with more example phrasings of chargeback and dispute requests.

questions.question: A billing dispute session was paused yesterday. Overnight, the billing team corrected the order record and applied a partial credit, so the session’s saved tool results are out of date. How should the agent continue the case?

options.text: Start a new session seeded with a structured summary of case facts and decisions, and let the agent re-query the tools.
Resume the session and tell the agent to call lookup_order and get_customer again before acting.
Fork the session with fork_session so the continuation runs in a new branch.
Resume the session by its stored ID so the agent keeps yesterday’s full context.

questions.question: A support agent runs on short-lived containers. Resuming a saved session ID fails on new containers because session files are local, and summaries injected into fresh sessions lost details. How should the team keep the full conversation across customer returns?

options.text: Resume the saved ID with fork_session so each container works on its own copy.
Start a fresh session each time with a longer structured summary of facts, decisions and quotes.
Add a SessionStore that mirrors session transcripts to shared storage, then resume by session ID on any container.
Set continue_conversation to true so each container picks up the most recent session.

questions.question: A team adds a PreToolUse hook that returns an allow decision for process_refund calls under $25, but those calls are still blocked. A deny rule matching process_refund remains from an earlier pilot. What should change?

options.text: Run these sessions in bypassPermissions mode.
Add process_refund to the agent’s allowedTools.
Move the auto-approval into a PostToolUse hook.
Remove the deny rule that matches process_refund from the permission settings.

questions.question: For complex disputes, a support coordinator spawns two parallel subagents, one for billing history and one for order records. Each independently calls get_customer and lookup_order for the same customer, and resolution latency is at its limit. How do you remove the duplication?

options.text: Add a shared state store where each subagent logs fetched data for the other to reuse.
Run the subagents in sequence, passing the first’s results into the second’s prompt.
Have the coordinator call get_customer and lookup_order once and include the results in each subagent’s prompt.
Merge both subagents into one investigation agent.

questions.question: A complex dispute involves a duplicate charge and a missing replacement order. The coordinator spawns two parallel subagents with vague, overlapping prompts, and both investigate the duplicate charge, nearly doubling token use and producing conflicting findings. Resolution time is already at its limit. What change is most effective?

options.text: Let the subagents report their focus areas to each other while they run.
Have the coordinator split the dispute into distinct issues before delegating, giving each subagent one issue with explicit scope boundaries.
Run the subagents in sequence, passing the first one’s findings to the second.
Keep the prompts and have the coordinator remove duplicate and conflicting findings when merging.

questions.question: A research system’s web search subagent twice ran shell commands embedded in fetched pages, despite a prompt rule to treat page content as data. The subagent needs only fetch tools. Which change guarantees embedded instructions can’t execute commands?

options.text: Restrict the search subagent’s AgentDefinition tool list to web fetch and read tools, removing Bash and Write.
Have the coordinator restate the untrusted-content rule in every delegation prompt.
Add a PostToolUse hook that strips text that looks like instructions from each fetched page.
Enable strict tool use so every tool call is validated against its schema.

questions.question: A web search subagent emits register_source and add_citation in one turn. add_citation needs the source ID that register_source returns, and register_source fails because the URL is unreachable. The subagent also runs independent searches in parallel, and you want to keep that. How should the loop handle the pending add_citation call?

options.text: Resend with disable_parallel_tool_use true so the two calls arrive in separate turns.
Run add_citation with a placeholder source ID to correct later.
Return the register_source error alone and send no tool_result for add_citation.
Return a tool_result for add_citation with is_error true and a short note that its prerequisite failed.

questions.question: An engineer ran several named investigation sessions last week, one per pipeline bug, plus short unrelated sessions since. No files have changed, and they can’t remember the exact name of the session they need. How do they reopen it?

options.text: Run claude –continue to reopen the most recent conversation in the directory.
Start a new session and paste a summary of the investigation’s key findings.
Run claude –resume with the closest name they remember.
Run claude –resume without a session argument and choose the investigation from the interactive picker.

questions.question: A citation-verification step uses the Messages API Tool Runner with client tools. One run kept repeating fetch_url calls and never finished. The team wants a guaranteed bound on every run and correct completion detection. What should they change?

options.text: Set max_iterations on the runner as a safety cap and treat a run that stops at the cap as incomplete.
Set max_iterations to the usual number of tool calls and treat stopping at the cap as a normal finish.
Detect repeated identical tool calls in the harness and abort when that pattern appears.
Replace the runner with a manual loop that stops when stop_reason is end_turn.

questions.question: In a research refinement loop, the synthesis subagent checks its own output for coverage gaps and requests follow-up research. Finished reports still miss subtopics, and the agent rates its coverage as complete. Which change fixes the loop?

options.text: Have the synthesis subagent output a per-subtopic coverage rating and trigger research below a threshold.
Enable extended thinking for the synthesis subagent’s self-review.
Add a review subagent that scores each finished report and appends the gaps it finds.
Have the coordinator compare each synthesis output with the subtopic decomposition and re-delegate research for uncovered subtopics.

questions.question: A support agent’s code gate blocks process_refund until get_customer has verified someone in the session. An audit found a refund posted to an order that had nothing to do with the verified caller. What should the gate check?

options.text: That the order in the refund call belongs to the same customer that get_customer verified.
That get_customer returned a verified result within ten minutes before the refund call.
That the order ID came from a lookup_order call made after get_customer in the same session.
That the caller repeats their full name and email just before the refund is submitted.

questions.question: Policy lets a support agent post refunds up to $20 on its own; larger ones need a person. The team enforces this with a PreToolUse callback hook on process_refund in the Agent SDK. Which two design choices are best? (select two)

options.text: Deny calls over $20 with a reason telling the agent to route the case through escalate_to_human.
Let calls over $20 run, and add a PostToolUse hook that flags each one for supervisor review.
Return updatedInput with the amount reduced to $20 so a partial refund posts without review.
Read the refund amount from the hook’s tool_input, not from the amount the customer stated earlier.

questions.question: An analyst asks a research coordinator for ’the latest merger numbers.’ Two mergers she covers are pending, so the coordinator ends its turn asking which one, and the loop records the run as failed. What should happen instead?

options.text: Pick the merger with the most recent regulator filing and state that assumption at the top of the brief.
Pass the coordinator’s question to the analyst, then send her reply back in the next user message.
Keep the failed status and send runs that end without a brief to a support queue.
Pick one merger, draft its brief, and ask in the first line whether it was the right one.

questions.question: Yesterday, Claude’s Bash tool started a local mock of a carrier API in the background on port 8081. Today the engineer resumes that session by its ID on the same laptop, Claude calls the mock at that address, and every call fails. What should she do?

options.text: Resume with fork_session so the new branch restarts the processes the original session started.
Use continue instead of resume to reopen the latest session with its earlier processes.
Restart the mock on its original port, then tell the resumed session it’s running again.
Restart the mock on the next free port and have Claude retry its earlier calls exactly as before.

questions.question: An investigation started in Claude Code on one engineer’s laptop. Tonight the on-call team must carry it on from a shared server where the same repository is already cloned. How should the work carry over?

options.text: Run claude –resume on the server with the laptop session’s ID.
Run claude –continue on the server to pick up the most recent conversation.
Commit a handoff file, then resume the laptop session by its ID on the server.
Start a new server session seeded with a structured note of confirmed findings, open questions and next steps.

questions.question: A CI step’s claude -p run with –output-format json returns a session_id. A later step, in a new process on a shared runner, must ask a follow-up about that review. What should it do?

options.text: Start a new claude -p run and paste the earlier JSON output into its prompt.
Save session_id from the first step’s output and pass it to –resume in the follow-up run.
Run the follow-up with –continue to reopen the latest conversation on the runner.
Run with –continue –fork-session to branch from the latest conversation.

questions.question: A review coordinator creates one subagent per changed hunk, spawning 300 subagents for a 40-file pull request. An earlier single-pass version missed interactions between related modules. How should the review be divided?

options.text: Group related files or concerns into a few focused passes, then run one integration pass that checks how they interact.
Keep one subagent per hunk but launch them in batches of twenty.
Go back to one pass over the whole diff and allow a longer answer.
Give each module its own subagent and let each one report issues in other modules it touches.

questions.question: process_refund succeeded, but its confirmation reached the support agent late, and the agent proposed the same refund again. Payments can’t be reversed, and network delays sometimes deliver duplicate requests. Which two controls should run before any further refund call on this order? (select two)

options.text: Look up the refund state by order or transaction ID in the payment system before accepting the call.
Check the conversation history for an earlier refund confirmation.
Reject a new refund when the same amount was sent in the last few minutes.
Reject any new refund for an order or transaction ID that already has a completed refund on record.

questions.question: Claude Code maintains an extraction mapper. After an edit, the same type error keeps coming back while Claude moves on without running the type check. The team wants each type error reported right after the edit that caused it. Which hook fits best?

options.text: A PreToolUse hook on edit tools that runs the type check before each edit.
A PostToolUse hook on edit tools that runs the full test suite and logs the results.
A Stop hook that runs the type check when Claude finishes and blocks completion on errors.
A PostToolUse hook on edit tools that runs the type check after each edit and returns any failure to Claude.

questions.question: A third-party MCP tool returns invoices as JSON text with invoice_id, amount in cents and due_date. A PostToolUse hook uses updatedToolOutput so Claude sees amounts in dollars, and Claude later passes each invoice_id to a pay_invoice tool. How should the hook build the replacement?

options.text: Return a short prose summary of the converted totals.
Return the same JSON structure with every field kept and only the amount values converted.
Return only the converted amounts, since the other fields are already in context.
Return the converted JSON alongside the original under a new top-level key.

questions.question: A research search subagent’s last message reads: “Done. Found 14 relevant sources; details above.” The coordinator then has no sources to pass on, and the brief stalls. What should change?

options.text: Require the final message to contain all findings in full, including each source’s URL, key claim and date.
Give the coordinator read access to the search subagent’s full transcript.
Have the coordinator read any files the search subagent saved and rebuild the list.
Stream the subagent’s intermediate messages to the coordinator while it runs.

questions.question: A team prefers given/when/then names for generated tests but accepts exceptions when another name reads better. An engineer proposes a PreToolUse hook that blocks any Write whose test names don’t match a pattern. What fits best?

options.text: Put the naming preference and one example test name in CLAUDE.md or the tests rule file.
Add the hook with an error message showing a correctly named example.
Add a PostToolUse hook that renames tests to match the pattern after each Write.
Fail the CI build on any non-matching name and have developers rename tests by hand.

questions.question: A CI test-writing job runs one long prompt chain for every pull request, covering API, UI, migration and docs changes. Docs-only changes still take nine minutes and get irrelevant test suggestions. What fits best?

options.text: Add a first step listing the changed file types and pass it through the same full chain.
Run the API, UI, migration and docs chains in parallel on every pull request and merge.
Skip test writing for pull requests under 20 changed lines.
Classify each pull request by kind of change first, then run the chain built for that kind.

questions.question: Each vuln-db advisory is about 8,000 tokens. Policy requires every full advisory to be kept for audit, but reviews need only severity, affected versions and fixed version. What fits best?

options.text: A PreToolUse hook that logs each lookup request, plus a PostToolUse hook that trims results.
A PostToolUse hook that trims each advisory to three fields; auditors re-query vuln-db for details.
A PostToolUse hook that appends a three-field summary to each full advisory.
A PostToolUse hook that saves the full advisory to audit storage, then passes Claude only the three fields.

questions.question: For a PR touching six endpoints, a test-writing job plans one test file per endpoint. After writing two, it finds the PR also changed shared auth middleware that all six call, which its plan never covered. What should it do next?

options.text: Finish the four remaining files as planned and note the middleware change in the summary.
Stop and fail the job so a developer can split the pull request.
Add a seventh test file for the middleware, then finish the remaining four as planned.
Replan the remaining work around the middleware change and revisit the two test files already written.

questions.question: Each customs declaration is extracted, validated and submitted, and the customs authority charges a penalty for every amended declaration. A specialist reviews the day’s submissions each evening and often finds errors that passed validation. What should change?

options.text: Move the specialist’s review to just before submission and hold each declaration until it is approved.
Keep the evening review and add a process for filing corrections early the next day.
Add a second Claude instance before submission and retire the specialist’s review.
Add validation rules for the errors found each evening and block declarations that fail them.

questions.question: Policy lets refunds up to $250 run automatically; anything larger needs a supervisor’s approval for the full amount. A customer asks for $900 for a damaged sofa and suggests four smaller refunds. Today process_refund checks each call against $250 on its own. What should change?

options.text: Move the $250 check into a PreToolUse hook that compares each call’s amount with the limit.
Track the cumulative amount refunded for the case and send the full $900 for supervisor approval before any payment.
Issue $250 now automatically and send the remaining $650 for approval afterward.
Keep the per-call check and reject a second refund on the same order within 24 hours.

questions.question: A support agent called lookup_order five times in a row with the same order ID; each result said “in transit, next update 18:00,” and the customer added nothing new. What should the application do?

options.text: Have the agent wait until 18:00 before its next lookup, then continue the loop.
Set max_turns to 5 so the loop ends and the case closes after five calls.
Cache lookup_order results for an hour so repeated calls are faster.
Detect repeated identical calls with identical results, then end the loop with an escalation that carries the order status.

questions.question: Policy requires a carrier claim, filed with file_carrier_claim, before a support agent finishes any damaged-delivery case. The agent sometimes ends its turn without filing one, and the team wants a deterministic check at completion. Which hook fits?

options.text: A PreToolUse hook on escalate_to_human that blocks handoffs until a claim is on file.
A PostToolUse hook on process_refund that files the claim automatically after each refund.
A Stop hook that checks for a filed claim and blocks completion with a reason until one exists.
A SubagentStop hook that checks for a claim when the claims subagent finishes.

questions.question: Three search subagents each studied one district’s vaccination data for this week’s report, and each returned cited findings. The report leaves out the Eastfield district, including a 12-point drop, although the coordinator’s log shows Eastfield’s result arrived complete with the finding and citation. Which two actions should the team take? (select two)

options.text: Trace the Eastfield result ID from the coordinator through the synthesis-input records to find the exact handoff that failed.
Rerun the Eastfield search with broader terms and replace its result before regenerating.
Require synthesis to confirm one outcome record per assigned district before drafting: cited findings or a documented failure.
Raise synthesis’s token budget and regenerate, assuming the late findings were truncated.

questions.question: A research coordinator loops: search for more sources, then ask a reviewer whether the report is complete. The reviewer keeps finding new gaps, and last week the loop ran nine rounds and missed the deadline. Which two changes fix this? (select two)

options.text: Define exit criteria in advance, such as two sources for each key question, and stop once they’re met.
Cap the loop at three rounds and escalate any remaining gaps to a human analyst with a summary of what was tried.
Let the reviewer decide when the report is complete, with a stricter definition of complete.
Allow new gaps each round, but require each gap to cite a missing source.

questions.question: An analyst resumes Tuesday’s session. The brief’s admissions total and its admissions per 1,000 residents both come from the county admissions file; ambulance response times come from a separate dispatch file. Only the admissions file has been corrected since. What is the most targeted instruction?

options.text: Name the admissions file, have the agent re-read it and update the total, keeping the other findings.
Name the admissions file, have the agent re-read it and recheck both the total and the per-1,000 rate.
Name the file, have the agent re-read it and recheck every figure in the summary table.
Paste the corrected count into the prompt and have the agent substitute it in the total and the rate.

questions.question: For each report, a coordinator pastes the full text of a 300-page health survey into the prompts of five analysis subagents. Their context fills early and costs have tripled. Which two changes fix this? (select two)

options.text: Summarize the whole survey in the coordinator and paste the summary into each subagent prompt.
Give each subagent the file path and the page range it covers, and let it read those pages with Read.
Store the extracted text once and pass a document ID that each subagent uses to fetch only the sections it needs.
Remove line breaks and tables from the text before pasting it into each prompt.

questions.question: Council analysts use a research agent through a web app built on the TypeScript Agent SDK. When Claude calls AskUserQuestion, the canUseTool callback shows the questions as buttons. After the analyst clicks, it returns allow with the original input, and Claude carries on as if nothing was answered. What should the callback return?

options.text: Allow with updatedInput holding an answers array of the chosen labels in question order.
Allow with updatedInput whose options are trimmed to the chosen label.
Allow with updatedInput holding the original questions plus an answers object keyed by question text.
Allow with no updatedInput, after storing the selections on the session.

questions.question: Two new rules apply to a research document subagent: it must never call delete_document, and it may call fetch_url only for domains on an allowlist that the legal team updates in a database several times a day. Which setup fits both rules?

options.text: State both rules in the system prompt and log every call for a weekly review.
Add a PreToolUse hook for delete_document and a static list of today’s allowed domains.
Add permission deny rules for delete_document and for every domain not currently on the allowlist.
Add a permission deny rule for delete_document, and a PreToolUse hook that checks each fetch_url domain against the database.

questions.question: About 40% of requests to a research system are single-fact questions, such as a regulation’s effective date, answerable from one source. Each still goes through the coordinator and four subagents, taking three minutes and many more tokens than a direct lookup. Answers are accurate. What should the team do?

options.text: Route single-fact questions to one agent with search and citation tools, and keep the full pipeline for research reports.
Run the four subagents in parallel for single-fact questions so answers arrive sooner.
Replace the four subagents with one larger subagent for every request type.
Send single-fact questions straight to the search subagent, skipping the coordinator but keeping synthesis and reporting.

questions.question: A research report requested on data-privacy rules in the EU, the US and Japan covers only the EU and the US. Japan isn’t mentioned anywhere, not even as a coverage gap. What should the team inspect first?

options.text: The coordinator’s delegation log, to see whether any task asked a subagent to cover Japan.
The search subagent’s queries, to see whether any used Japanese terms or sources.
The synthesis subagent’s inputs and outputs, to see whether Japan findings were dropped.
The report subagent’s settings, to see whether a length limit cut off a Japan section.

questions.question: An analyst forks her research session twice to draft two report versions. Later, in the original session, she says one dataset was revised and gives the new figures. Both drafts still use the old figures. What should she do?

options.text: Send the revised figures to each forked session directly, because a fork shares history only up to the moment it was created.
Resume each fork with –continue to pull in messages added to the original later.
Wait for automatic compaction to merge newer parent messages into each fork.
Fork the original twice again and throw away both drafts.

questions.question: Each pull request summary must follow nine house rules, such as a 120-word limit, a Risks section and a linked ticket. Summaries read well but each breaks one or two rules, and different ones each time. What should the job do?

options.text: Generate the summary first, then run a second step that checks it against all nine rules and corrects any violations.
Move the nine rules to the end of the prompt, after the diff.
Reject any violating summary and regenerate it from scratch with the same prompt until one passes.
Split the rules across nine prompts, each generating its own version.

questions.question: A hook blocks change_plan until get_customer has verified the caller’s account PIN. When it blocks, the support agent sees only “Denied,” then retries change_plan or tells the customer the system is down. What should the hook return when it blocks?

options.text: A reason saying the request was denied by policy, with no detail.
Nothing different; add a system prompt instruction to escalate on any denial.
A reason saying the caller must be verified first, without naming the verification tool.
A reason saying the account PIN is unverified and that get_customer must verify it before change_plan can run.

questions.question: An engineer asks Claude Code to update a booking API, its client SDK, the developer docs and the mobile app for a new cancellation rule. Claude delegates three subagent tasks and reports the work done, but the mobile app was never touched. Which two steps prevent this? (select two)

options.text: Before delegating, have Claude list the request’s required parts and check that each one is covered by a task.
Give each subagent the full original request so it can pick up any part nobody else covers.
Have each subagent report the files it changed and have Claude summarize them.
After the subagents return, have Claude check the combined results against every part of the original request.

questions.question: A documentation workflow always runs four fixed steps on each module: read it, write an API reference, write a tutorial and write a migration guide. For internal helper modules, the tutorial and migration guide come out as filler that reviewers delete. Which two changes fit? (select two)

options.text: Let Claude decide which documentation pieces each module needs after reading it, and produce only those.
Keep a fixed first step that inventories the module’s public API, and base the later steps on what it finds.
Keep all four steps and have Claude write “not applicable” when a section doesn’t fit.
Split the chain into four skills and run all four on every module in parallel.

questions.question: An engineer uses one Claude Code session all day: a booking bug in the morning, CSS fixes after lunch, then a reporting query. By evening, answers borrow assumptions from the booking bug, such as its test fixtures. Which two habits fit? (select two)

options.text: Run /compact before each new task so earlier work is condensed but carried forward.
Run /clear before starting an unrelated task so it begins with an empty context.
Start a new session for each unrelated task and resume an older one later only if needed.
Keep one session and state at the top of each prompt which task it belongs to.

questions.question: Before a test-generation job finishes, two checks must run: every generated test must pass the test runner, and each test must check a stated requirement rather than restate the current code. Which setup fits?

options.text: A command hook that runs the test runner, and a prompt-based hook in which a model judges whether the tests match the stated requirements.
A command hook for both checks, with a script that searches test names for keywords from the requirements.
A prompt-based hook for both, asking a model to predict whether the tests would pass.
Instructions in CLAUDE.md asking Claude to confirm both checks in its final message.

questions.question: A review coordinator spends 30 turns weighing findings, rejecting some and recording why. It then starts a new subagent to write the final summary comment, and the summary lists rejected findings as open. The summary depends on nearly all of that discussion. How should the summary step start?

options.text: As a fresh subagent told to “summarize the decisions we made,” with the PR number.
As a fresh subagent given only the diff, so it reconstructs the decisions independently.
As a fresh subagent with read access to the coordinator’s transcript file.
By resuming the coordinator’s session with fork_session, so the summary starts with the full discussion, including every rejection and its reason.

questions.question: An extraction loop treats any stop_reason other than tool_use as a finished answer. Some saved records are truncated JSON, and a few contain refusal text instead of data. What should the loop do?

options.text: Treat end_turn and max_tokens the same but validate JSON before saving.
Retry any non-tool_use response three times and save the last result.
Retry max_tokens with a higher limit and save refusals and end_turn responses as records.
Handle each stop_reason separately: retry max_tokens with a higher limit, send refusals to review and save only end_turn results.

questions.question: An extractor handles 40-page contracts. On one contract, 38 fields are clear but two clauses need a lawyer’s judgment, and the current workflow sends the whole contract to legal review and extracts nothing. What should happen?

options.text: Extract the 38 fields, publish the record as complete, and send the two clauses to legal separately.
Extract the 38 clear fields and send only the two clauses to legal review, marking the record pending on those two fields until a lawyer decides.
Extract all 40 fields, using Claude’s best reading of the two clauses with a low-confidence flag.
Extract the 38 fields, leave the two clauses null and let downstream users request review.

questions.question: A team’s hand-written Messages API loop now has custom code for tool execution, validation hooks before each tool call, retries and resuming interrupted sessions, and maintaining it takes a day a week. What should the team consider?

options.text: Moving to the Claude Agent SDK, whose managed agent loop includes these features.
Adopting the SDK Tool Runner, which automates the tool-call loop.
Keeping the loop and adding prompt caching to cut its cost.
Moving to Claude Code hooks, which add checks before tool calls.

questions.question: A pipeline chooses an extraction tool with a hand-written decision tree that checks keywords, such as “Invoice” in the first line. It now has 40 branches, and documents with unusual layouts still go to the wrong tool. What should the team do?

options.text: Give Claude the extraction tools with clear descriptions and let it choose one after reading each document.
Add branches for each unusual layout found in production and review the tree monthly.
Replace the tree with a trained classifier, which first needs about 10,000 labeled documents.
Send every document to every tool and keep the first output that passes validation.

questions.question: A research system’s synthesis subagent must report every finding by calling one of three tools: record_statistic, record_quote or record_narrative, each with its own schema. On a model that supports forced tool use, some runs return plain text instead of a tool call and the coordinator’s parser fails. What is the correct fix?

options.text: Keep tool_choice as “auto” and add a system prompt rule that every finding must be reported through a tool.
Set tool_choice to {“type”: “tool”, “name”: “record_narrative”} on the subagent’s requests.
Set tool_choice to {“type”: “any”} on the synthesis subagent’s requests.
Add strict: true to all three recording tool definitions so their inputs follow each schema.

questions.question: A research system’s document analysis subagent spends its first few tool calls finding out which research collections exist and which fields each one has. The collections change daily. Which two changes give the subagent this information without spending tool calls on discovery? (select two)

options.text: Write the current list of collections and their fields into each subagent’s system prompt.
Expose the collection inventory as an MCP resource that lists every collection and its fields.
Define a resource template such as docs://collections/{id}/schema for each collection’s field details.
Add a describe_collections tool that returns the current inventory of collections and their fields.

questions.question: A research system’s document analysis subagent must run extract_metadata before any enrichment tool. After the metadata result comes back, it may call enrichment tools or finish with a text answer. On a model that supports forced tool use, which two tool_choice settings implement this? (select two)

options.text: Switch tool_choice to {“type”: “none”} on follow-up requests once the metadata result is returned.
Set tool_choice to {“type”: “tool”, “name”: “extract_metadata”} on the first request.
Switch tool_choice to {“type”: “auto”} on follow-up requests once the metadata result is returned.
Set tool_choice to {“type”: “any”} on every request in the pipeline.

questions.question: A research system’s web search tool fails for three reasons: rate limits, queries over the length limit and paywalled sources. Every failure returns is_error: true with only “search failed”. The subagent retries paywalled sources and gives up on rate-limited queries. What fixes its recovery decisions?

options.text: Return a different error message for each cause, saying what failed and what to try next.
Intercept error tool results in the Tool Runner and retry them there before the model sees them.
Have the coordinator retry every failed search twice with exponential backoff before logging a coverage gap.
Add a system prompt rule listing which search failure causes can be retried and which can’t.

questions.question: The synthesis subagent must collect every findings file. File names start with findings- and end in .md or .json. The files sit at any depth under work/, contents vary, and there are fewer than 40. Which two approaches find all of them? (select two)

options.text: Call Glob once with the pattern work/*/findings-*.{md,json}.
Call Glob once with the pattern work/**/findings-*.{md,json}.
Call Grep across work/ with the pattern findings- and collect the files that match.
Call Glob twice, once with work/**/findings-*.md and once with work/**/findings-*.json.

questions.question: A synthesis subagent calls verify_claim on almost every turn, even for claims that already cite a source. The tool description is detailed and has clear boundaries. The system prompt says: “CRITICAL: You MUST use verify_claim.” What fixes the over-triggering?

options.text: Add stronger boundary language to the verify_claim description, stating when the tool should not be used.
Set tool_choice to auto for the synthesis subagent so the model decides whether each turn needs a tool.
Rewrite the system prompt instruction as targeted criteria, such as “Use verify_claim when a claim lacks a source.”
Remove verify_claim from the synthesis subagent and route all verification through the coordinator.

questions.question: Each research subagent’s tools are scoped to its role. Now the synthesis agent often needs to confirm a single fact (a date, a figure) that is missing from its handed-off findings, and each check costs a full round trip through the coordinator to the search agent. What is the recommended change?

options.text: Give the synthesis agent a constrained verify_fact lookup tool and keep complex research with the coordinator.
Pass the search agent’s full raw results, not summaries, in the context at delegation.
Have the coordinator spawn several search subagents in parallel to run the checks as one batch.
Give the synthesis agent the full web search toolset so it can fill gaps itself.

questions.question: A research system needs two new integrations: standard Jira task tracking, and the team’s internal archive of past reports, which has a proprietary API that no public MCP server supports. Which two integration decisions are correct? (select two)

options.text: Document the archive’s API endpoints in CLAUDE.md and have agents call them with Bash.
Build a custom MCP server that wraps the internal archive’s proprietary API.
Build a custom Jira MCP server whose tools encode the team’s ticket-filing conventions.
Connect Jira through an existing community MCP server.

questions.question: A security scan finds a live GitHub token in the committed .mcp.json. The server is a local stdio server started with npx that reads the token from its env entry. The team rotates the token, and configuration changes must still reach developers through version control. What is the correct fix?

options.text: Change the entry to ${GITHUB_TOKEN:-<rotated token>} so developers who haven’t set the variable still connect.
Configure a headersHelper script that outputs the token as a dynamic header, so no credential sits in the file.
Replace the token with a ${GITHUB_TOKEN} reference in the server’s env entry and have developers set the variable locally.
Add an Authorization header of Bearer ${GITHUB_TOKEN} under the server’s headers field and remove the env entry.

questions.question: A pull request changes parseAmount in src/utils/money.ts, and src/utils/index.ts re-exports it as toCents. The review currently greps only for parseAmount and misses call sites. Which two steps find every affected caller? (select two)

options.text: Read src/utils/index.ts to list every name the function is exported under.
Grep for the import path utils/money to find every file that imports the module.
Grep file contents for each exported name, including the toCents alias.
Glob for a pattern like **/*parseAmount* to find files that reference the function.

questions.question: An agent harness sends its first request with tool_choice {“type”: “tool”, “name”: “get_code_conventions”} (on a model that supports forced tool use) so generated code follows team conventions. The response ends with stop_reason “tool_use”, and no conventions data appears anywhere. What must the harness do next?

options.text: Return the tool_result in the next request but keep tool_choice forced to get_code_conventions.
Run get_code_conventions, append a tool_result with the tool call’s ID and send the updated history in a new request.
Turn the tool’s output into a plain user text message and append that to the history.
Do nothing more; the API runs the forced tool and returns its output in the same response.

questions.question: A developer-productivity agent’s find_known_issues MCP tool returns an empty list both on a database timeout and on a real no-match. Maintenance windows take the database offline for minutes, so the agent reports modules as issue-free. The harness marks a call as failed only when the tool result itself signals failure. How should the tool report timeouts?

options.text: Add a status field set to timeout or no_matches inside the normal result body for the agent to check.
Return timeouts with isError: true and a descriptive message, and keep the empty list for genuine no-matches.
Log each timeout to the server’s monitoring dashboard and alert the database maintainers.
Retry the query inside the server with exponential backoff and respond only after a retry succeeds.

questions.question: A documentation MCP server’s catalog gains and loses resource entries many times a day, but each document’s content rarely changes after publication. Long agent sessions keep trying to read URIs that no longer exist. Which server change fixes this?

options.text: Return an empty contents array from resources/read for removed URIs so the agent can detect the gap.
Advertise the resources.listChanged capability and send notifications/resources/list_changed when entries are added or removed.
Advertise resources.subscribe so the client receives notifications/resources/updated for resources it follows.
Add a system prompt rule telling the agent to call resources/list again before every resources/read.

questions.question: A developer is testing an unstable, daily-changing MCP server for semantic code search. The team shares three MCP servers through a version-controlled .mcp.json, and teammates must not get the experimental one. Where should it be configured?

options.text: In .mcp.json, with .mcp.json added to the repository’s .gitignore.
In .mcp.json, loading its token through ${SEARCH_TOKEN} environment variable expansion.
As launch commands and arguments in the developer’s uncommitted local CLAUDE.md.
In the developer’s ~/.claude.json, at user or local scope.

questions.question: A developer-productivity agent’s UI must show a short text explanation beside each suggest_refactor call. Since the team set tool_choice to {“type”: “any”}, responses contain tool_use blocks but no text, despite prompt instructions. What restores the explanations?

options.text: Change tool_choice to {“type”: “tool”, “name”: “suggest_refactor”} and keep the instruction in the prompt.
Add disable_parallel_tool_use: true to limit each response to one tool call.
Keep tool_choice “any” and add a stronger system prompt rule requiring text before the call.
Set tool_choice to {“type”: “auto”} and tell the model in the prompt to always call suggest_refactor.

questions.question: After resolving a case, a support agent must change ‘status: open’ to ‘status: resolved’ in that case’s entry in its notes file. It knows the entry only by its position. Edit fails because the anchor text appears in every templated entry, and a longer anchor with neighboring lines still matches several entries because they are identical. What should the agent do next?

options.text: Use Read to load the full file, then Write the complete content with that one entry updated.
Keep the same old_string and rerun Edit with replace_all set to true.
Extend old_string again until it spans enough of the file to match only once.
Use Bash to run a sed command that replaces the status line at the entry’s position.

questions.question: A support agent gets four backend tools from one MCP server. You add an investigation subagent that should use only get_customer and lookup_order, and process_refund must not be available to it at all. Which configuration achieves this?

options.text: In the subagent’s configuration, set allowedTools to auto-approve only the two lookup tools by their full MCP names.
In the subagent’s definition, set the tools field to list only get_customer and lookup_order.
Add a permissions.deny rule that blocks the process_refund MCP tool by its full name.
Define the backend MCP server inline in the subagent’s frontmatter instead of in .mcp.json.
