questions.question: In failing support transcripts, the agent calls lookup_order for order details, then calls process_refund just to check eligibility, issuing unwanted refunds. The refund inputs are well formed, and both tools have one-line descriptions. What is the highest-leverage fix?

options.text: Add a PreToolUse hook that denies process_refund until lookup_order has returned in the session.
Add routing rules to the system prompt mapping each request type to the right backend tool.
Add input_examples to process_refund showing correctly formatted refund calls.
Rewrite the process_refund description to say it executes a refund and that eligibility checks belong to lookup_order.

questions.question: A support agent’s tools are split across two MCP servers: crm (get_customer, lookup_order) and billing (process_refund, escalate_to_human). Each team deploys its own server, and neither will maintain shared middleware. One refund conversation needs live calls to both. How should tool access be configured?

options.text: Build one aggregator MCP server that re-exposes both teams’ tools behind a single connection.
Register only the billing server and put current customer and order data in the system prompt.
Register both servers in the agent’s configuration; tools from both are available at the same time.
Register the billing server and add mcp__crm__* to allowedTools so the agent can call the crm tools.

questions.question: A find_owner MCP tool returns isError: true with “no owner found” in two cases: when the registry times out during its nightly 30-second rebuild, and when a file really has no registered owner. The agent retries ownerless files and gives up during rebuilds, and the harness stops any tool call after 10 seconds. Which two response changes fix the agent’s recovery? (select two)

options.text: For a registry timeout, keep isError: true and include errorCategory “transient” and isRetryable: true in the error content.
For a file with no registered owner, return a successful result with an empty owner field.
For a file with no registered owner, return isError: true with errorCategory “validation” and a note to re-check the path.
For a registry timeout, retry inside the tool with backoff until the rebuild finishes, then return the owner.

questions.question: An engineer asks the agent to list every call to the legacy helper cache.flushAll() in the repository. The review needs each matching line with its line number. Which Grep call is correct?

options.text: Pattern cache.flushAll( with output_mode set to content.
Pattern cache.flushAll( with output_mode set to content.
Pattern cache.flushAll( with output_mode set to count.
Pattern cache.flushAll( with output_mode left at its default.

questions.answerNote: Supplied HTML renders choices A and B identically. Original regex escaping is missing; no unique correct option can be established.

questions.question: A support agent gets a new track_shipment tool described as “Gets order and delivery information”, while lookup_order is described as “Retrieves order information.” Delivery questions still go to lookup_order even after a routing rule was added to the system prompt. What fixes the misrouting most directly?

options.text: Expand the routing rule with few-shot examples of the right tool for each request type.
Add input_examples to both tools with typical order and tracking identifiers.
Classify messages for delivery keywords and force track_shipment with tool_choice for those.
Rewrite each tool’s description to state what it returns, when to use it and when the other tool applies.

questions.question: To investigate billing disputes, a team gave its support agent a generic run_query tool that runs any SQL string. Some queries return rows belonging to other customers, even though they touch only billing tables. What is the correct redesign?

options.text: Have the harness scan run_query results and remove rows whose customer_id doesn’t match.
Replace run_query with a get_billing_history tool that takes a verified customer_id and a date range.
Add a PreToolUse hook that blocks run_query calls referencing tables outside the billing schema.
Expand the run_query description with a rule that every query must filter on the current customer ID.

questions.question: Reports attach wrong source URLs only to citations that come through the document-ingestion path. Tests show the shared citation formatter renders correctly when given correct URL metadata. An earlier attempt used Read on dozens of files and ran out of context. Which exploration strategy is correct?

options.text: Grep for the document-ingestion citation symbols to find entry points, then Read those files and follow their imports.
Read the pipeline’s main entry file in full and trace the flow from that one file.
Read the citation formatter’s source in full and fix its URL handling before exploring ingestion.
Glob for all pipeline source files, then Read each file returned.

questions.question: A research system’s load_document tool rejects any source not on the approved citation list, with no exceptions, and subagents can’t read the list. MCP tools report failures with isError: true and a JSON body following your team’s schema: errorCategory, retriable and message. The tool currently returns only “Request denied.” The subagent retries the same URL repeatedly, then reports an outage. Which error body fixes both behaviors?

options.text: errorCategory “business” and retriable false, with a message saying the source isn’t on the approved list.
A successful result with an empty document body and a note that the source was skipped.
errorCategory “validation” and retriable true, suggesting a retry with a different URL from the approved list.
errorCategory “permission” and retriable false, telling the agent to escalate to a human reviewer.

questions.question: A research system’s report subagent must correct one citation line in a draft. Edit fails because the identical line appears in five places and only one should change. Which two recovery approaches are valid? (select two)

options.text: Call Write with only the corrected line and let Write merge it into the existing file.
Retry Edit with a longer anchor that includes surrounding lines, so the match becomes unique.
Use Read to load the whole file, then Write the complete corrected content back.
Run Edit with the replace-all option so every match is updated at once.

questions.question: An agent must update a retry limit that appears exactly once in config.ts. It must also regenerate scaffold.ts from a template, and some repositories don’t have scaffold.ts yet. Which two tool choices match each tool’s documented purpose? (select two)

options.text: Use Edit on config.ts, matching the single line that sets the retry limit.
Use Write on config.ts, passing only the updated retry-limit line as the file content.
Use Write on scaffold.ts, passing the complete generated file content.
Use Edit on scaffold.ts, matching its full current content and replacing it with the generated version.

questions.question: A research subagent reads the resource URI of a deleted document. The server returns a success result with an empty contents array, so the synthesis agent cites the document as empty. How should the server respond instead?

options.text: Return the read result with isError set and an errorCategory of business.
Return a JSON-RPC Invalid Params error (-32602) saying the resource doesn’t exist.
Advertise resources.subscribe so clients get notifications/resources/updated when a document is deleted.
Return one text content item that says the document wasn’t found.

questions.question: A team builds an MCP server for its shared citation database. Every contributor to this repository needs it, and it must not load in contributors’ unrelated projects. How should it be registered?

options.text: With local scope, so the configuration stays tied to this checkout.
In .mcp.json, keeping the file out of version control and documenting setup in the README.
At user scope in each contributor’s ~/.claude.json, following README steps.
With project scope, committing the resulting .mcp.json at the repository root.

questions.question: A search subagent gets find_content from the archive MCP server and search_content from the web server. Both descriptions already state clear boundaries, but archive queries still often go to the web tool. What reduces the misrouting most directly?

options.text: Force the archive tool with tool_choice naming find_content.
Add few-shot routing examples to the subagent’s system prompt.
Rename the tools with source prefixes, such as archive_find_documents and web_search_pages.
Add a select_search_tool routing tool that the subagent calls first.

questions.question: A synthesis agent’s scoped verify_fact tool handles frequent single-fact checks well. But when two sources disagree on a statistic, it makes long chains of verify_fact calls and still resolves the conflict wrongly. What is the correct design change?

options.text: Remove verify_fact and route every verification through the coordinator.
Have the synthesis agent return conflicts to the coordinator, which delegates the investigation to the web search agent.
Raise the synthesis agent’s tool-call budget so longer chains can finish.
Give the synthesis agent the web search agent’s full toolset.

questions.question: A document analysis subagent runs Glob with the pattern **/*.md to list every analysis note and gets 100 results plus a truncation flag. The notes/ folder holds about 400 notes in topic subfolders of fewer than 100 files each. What is the recommended way to get the complete list?

options.text: Run find through Bash across notes/ and parse its output.
Repeat the same Glob call until older files appear in a later result.
Use one Glob call with notes/**/*.md, excluding files outside notes/.
Call Glob once per topic subfolder, for example notes/economics/**/*.md, and merge the results.

questions.question: An engineer’s personal jira MCP server is user-scoped in ~/.claude.json and has the same name as the team’s jira entry in .mcp.json, so Claude Code connects only to the team version. Without editing the shared .mcp.json, which two changes make the personal build connect? (select two)

options.text: Delete the jira entry from the project’s .mcp.json so the user-scoped definition is used.
Re-add the personal build in that repository with claude mcp add at the default local scope.
Move the personal definition from ~/.claude.json into ~/.claude/settings.json to raise its precedence.
Rename the user-scoped server in ~/.claude.json to a name no project uses, such as jira-dev.

questions.question: A test-runner subagent uses Bash for test suites, linters and build scripts, and company policy says it must never run git push. Which configuration enforces this while keeping every other command working?

options.text: Replace Bash with a custom run_tests MCP tool that runs only the test suite.
Add a disallowedTools entry of Bash(git push *) to the subagent’s definition.
Add a Bash deny rule matching the git push pattern to permissions.deny.
List each approved Bash command pattern in the subagent’s allowedTools field.

questions.question: A project’s checked-in .mcp.json defines an HTTP code-index MCP server. Most engineers need the production URL ( https://code-index.internal/mcp ) with no setup, but a few run a local instance on a custom port. How should the url field be set?

options.text: ${CODE_INDEX_URL:-https://code-index.internal/mcp}, with local-instance engineers exporting CODE_INDEX_URL.
The production URL, with local-instance engineers defining the same server name in ~/.claude.json.
${CODE_INDEX_URL} without a default, with the production URL documented in the README.
The production URL committed, with local-instance engineers editing their copy of .mcp.json without committing.

questions.question: A support agent’s backend MCP server is remote over HTTP and needs a bearer token. Every engineer must get the server configuration through version control, and the secret must never be committed. Which two configuration decisions are correct? (select two)

options.text: Reference the token in the server’s headers, for example Authorization: Bearer ${SUPPORT_API_TOKEN}.
Declare the server entry with “type”: “http” together with its url.
Define the server in each engineer’s ~/.claude.json with the token referenced there.
Reference the token in headers as Authorization: Bearer ${ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN}.

questions.question: get_customer runs successfully against the authoritative customer database and finds no match for the well-formed email a customer gave. The agent retries the same call three times, then tells the customer the system is unavailable. Support policy allows one clarifying question before escalating. What behavior should you design?

options.text: Ask the customer for another identifier, such as an order number, and run a new lookup with it.
Call escalate_to_human with a handoff saying the customer’s identity couldn’t be verified.
Have get_customer return zero matches as isError true with errorCategory validation.
Add exponential backoff and a higher retry cap before the agent gives up.

questions.question: You plan to expose 40 refund and return policies through a support MCP server. The agent must see which policies exist without exploratory calls, and an engineer warns this will load every policy’s full text into context. Which design resolves the concern?

options.text: Advertise resources.listChanged so the server sends updated policy text into context when a policy changes.
Expose each policy as its own MCP resource; the agent reads one with resources/read only when a case needs it.
Expose a search_policies tool whose description covers each policy area and returns matching text.
Combine all 40 policies into one resource that the agent reads in full at the start of each session.

questions.question: An agent must list every case transcript file. Glob with **/*.json from the project root matched thousands of dependency files and was truncated. Transcripts live in data/transcripts/; completed ones contain a case_id field, but new cases start as empty placeholder files. What is the fix?

options.text: Use Read on the data/transcripts/ directory to get a listing.
Switch to Grep and search contents for case_id, collecting the matching paths.
Keep the **/*.json pattern and set Glob’s path parameter to data/transcripts/.
Run find data/transcripts -name ‘*.json’ through Bash and parse the output.

questions.question: A team is renaming lookup_order across an agent’s codebase. Before editing, it needs a count of references per source file, without adding hundreds of matching lines to context. Which approach is correct?

options.text: Grep with the default output mode and count the file paths returned.
Grep for lookup_order with output_mode set to count.
Grep with output_mode content and have the agent tally lines per file.
Glob with the pattern lookup_order to get per-file counts.

questions.question: A shared backend MCP server gives a support agent nine engineering tools, including run_sql_query. The agent answers some order questions with raw SQL rows instead of calling lookup_order, even after boundary language was added to the engineering tools’ descriptions. What should change?

options.text: Add a system prompt rule naming the four support tools as the only approved tools.
Rewrite run_sql_query’s description with example inputs and when-not-to-use guidance.
Restrict the agent’s allowed tools to the four support tools its role needs.
Force lookup_order with tool_choice whenever a message mentions an order.

questions.question: A server’s resources/list entries carry only a URI and names like doc-0481, so subagents read many irrelevant resources to find the right ones. Which two catalog changes let them choose correctly from the listing alone? (select two)

options.text: Add a preview_resource tool that returns the first lines of any URI.
Add icons to each entry and ttlMs cache metadata to the list response.
Add a description field to each resource entry saying what data it contains.
Fill in the title, mimeType and size fields on each resource entry.

questions.question: The first request forced extract_sources, and its result is back. The model must call verify_citations next, before any other tool or report text, and after verification later turns must be free to use the remaining tools. On a model that supports forced tool use, which two configurations guarantee verify_citations runs next without blocking later steps? (select two)

options.text: Send only verify_citations in the second request’s tools array, with tool_choice “auto”.
Set tool_choice to {“type”: “tool”, “name”: “verify_citations”} and keep it on every later request.
Set tool_choice to {“type”: “tool”, “name”: “verify_citations”} on the second request only.
Send only verify_citations in the second request’s tools array, with tool_choice {“type”: “any”}.

questions.question: A support agent’s lookup_order fails in three ways: ‘service busy’, ‘order not found’ and ‘permission denied’. Today the agent escalates every failure, and escalations have tripled. How should it handle the three errors?

options.text: Retry busy and not-found errors with exponential backoff, and escalate permission errors to a human.
Retry busy errors with backoff, escalate not-found errors, and ask the customer to recheck details on permission errors.
Retry busy errors with backoff, escalate not-found errors, and retry permission errors once after refreshing credentials.
Retry busy errors with backoff, ask the customer to confirm the order number on not-found errors, and escalate permission errors.

questions.question: In a bank’s research system, fetch_document returns ‘unsupported format’ for scanned regulator PDFs, which the subagent’s ocr_document tool can read. The subagent keeps calling fetch_document on the same filing until it hits its turn limit. What should the error contain?

options.text: A non-retryable error saying scans are unsupported, so the subagent skips the filing.
A retryable flag with a longer backoff so the service has time to convert the scan.
The raw parser exception with its stack trace and file size so the subagent can diagnose it.
A non-retryable error saying this tool can’t read scanned PDFs and naming ocr_document as the alternative.

questions.question: A research coordinator has all 18 tools of its four subagents in addition to its own. It often runs searches itself and fills its context, and the document subagent sometimes runs web searches outside its role. Which two changes address both problems? (select two)

options.text: Tell the coordinator in its prompt to prefer delegating, while it keeps all 18 tools.
Give each subagent only its role’s tools and let the coordinator keep all 18 to step in when needed.
Remove the search and document tools from the coordinator, leaving it the tools it needs to delegate.
Give each subagent only the tools its role requires, for example search tools for the search subagent.

questions.question: A codebase assistant’s repo-index search_code tool returns results like {id: ‘a91f3c’, ref: ‘x7’, t: 3}. The assistant often fetches the same file twice and can’t tell engineers who owns a result. Which output change helps most?

options.text: Return each result’s repository, file path, owning team and a short matching excerpt as clearly named fields.
Return repository and path as named fields and keep the owner in the short ID.
Keep the short IDs and add a decode_id tool to expand each identifier.
Keep the output and add a system prompt table that explains each short key.

questions.question: Logs show a codebase assistant doing all file work through Bash: cat to view files, sed to change them and npm test to run tests. Several sed edits corrupted YAML files, and cat on large files floods the context. What guidance fits?

options.text: Use Read to view files and keep sed for edits, running a YAML linter after each change.
Use Read to view files and Edit to change them, and keep Bash for builds and the test suite.
Keep Bash for tests and use Write to save each whole edited file after viewing it with cat.
Find code with Grep and Glob first, and keep Bash for sed edits and test runs.

questions.question: During a page, an engineer asks about a service last changed in spring. repo-index keeps one quarter of commits, but get_history’s description says only ‘Returns commit history for a file.’ It returns an empty list, and the assistant reports ’no recent changes.’ What helps most?

options.text: Document the tool’s retention window, what an empty result means and where older history can be found.
Rename it get_recent_history and add ‘covers recent commits’ to the description.
Add a system prompt rule to treat any empty result with suspicion and search again elsewhere.
Have get_history return an error for empty results so the assistant searches elsewhere.

questions.question: Claude must find every call to fetchRates whose options set retry: false. The calls span several lines, with “retry: false” two lines below “fetchRates(url, {”. Grep for fetchRates.*retry: false finds nothing. What should Claude do?

options.text: Add \n to the pattern between the two parts and search again.
Run the same Grep again with the multiline option enabled.
Use Glob to list files that mention fetchRates.
Escape the period and colon, then search again.

questions.question: The main session asked the Explore subagent to find a faulty date parser. Explore found it, proposed a three-line patch and reported the change as made, but git shows no modified files. What is the right next step?

options.text: Resume the same Explore instance with an allow rule for Edit so it applies the patch.
Hand Explore’s findings to an agent with write access that makes the edit and runs the tests.
Record the fix as done: subagent edits reach git only after the session ends.
Run Explore again in acceptEdits mode so its edits are approved automatically.

questions.question: A support platform exposes about 400 MCP tools. Their definitions take a large share of context on every turn, while five core tools are used on most turns and specialist tools only now and then. Which setup fits?

options.text: Keep the core tools loaded and defer the rest behind tool search.
Defer all tools, including the five core ones, behind tool search.
List the tool names in the prompt and fetch schemas on request.
Split the tools across three subagents that each load only their own group.

questions.question: A support agent is connected to 80 MCP tools from several teams and often picks a similarly named tool from a server the support workflow never uses. The support tools themselves work. What targets this most directly?

options.text: Add a prompt rule to prefer support tools whenever a customer mentions an order or refund.
Remove the servers this workflow never uses, then retest tool selection.
Keep all servers and put every tool behind tool search.
Keep all servers and deny only the three misused tools seen in last week’s logs.

questions.question: A jira MCP server exposes one tool, jira_op, with an op field (create, comment or transition) and a free-form payload. Calls often fail because the payload fields don’t fit the op. What fits best?

options.text: Add a JSON payload example for each op to the jira_op description and keep the single tool.
Validate payloads on the server and return an error listing the fields the chosen op expects.
Make op a required enum and add a system prompt table mapping each op to its fields.
Replace jira_op with one tool per operation, such as create_issue, each with an input schema that fits its payload.

questions.question: A repo-index server offers nine search tools, such as search_python and search_go, identical except for the language. The assistant often picks the wrong one, and cross-language searches need several calls. What fits best?

options.text: Add file extensions and example queries to all nine descriptions.
Load all nine through tool search with deferred loading.
Add a system prompt table mapping file extensions to tools.
Merge the nine tools into one search_code tool with a language parameter.

questions.question: Asked whether any code still calls fetchTariffs, a codebase assistant runs Grep for fetchTariffs with the glob *.ts, gets zero matches and says the function is safe to delete. Which two checks should come first? (select two)

options.text: Search again without the *.ts glob, so .tsx and .js files are covered too.
Ask the owning team whether anything still calls it and delete it if they know of none.
Search git history for commits mentioning fetchTariffs and check the files they changed.
Search for indirect references, such as re-exports under another name or lookups by the name as a string.

questions.question: An archive_search MCP server raises a JSON-RPC error when the upstream archive is down or licensing blocks a document. The agent gets no usable message, keeps calling the tool and never tries other sources. How should the server report these failures?

options.text: As a tool result with isError set, saying what failed and which other sources the agent could try.
Keep the JSON-RPC errors but add detailed codes the client can map to messages.
Return a normal empty result and let the agent decide to move on.
Retry inside the server until the archive responds, then return what it finds.

questions.question: An MCP server registers a new code-search tool while a session is running, and the client receives notifications/tools/list_changed on the existing connection. How should the client make the new tool available without dropping the connection?

options.text: Reconnect to the server so a fresh handshake returns the updated list.
Handle notifications/resources/list_changed and call resources/list for the new tools.
Call tools/list again on the existing connection and give Claude the updated definitions.
Send a new initialize request on the existing connection to get the current tool list.

questions.question: A nightly job runs claude -p with –mcp-config pointing at a JSON file whose remote tax-rate server entry has only a url field. The run exits cleanly, but no tax rate is ever looked up. Why?

options.text: Remote servers need command and args; add a command that starts a local client.
The server starts slowly; raise MCP_TIMEOUT so the run waits longer.
The entry has no transport type; Claude Code skips url entries without one at startup, so add type: http.
claude -p reads –mcp-config only with –bare; add –bare.

questions.question: After gathering facts, a final API call writes the customer’s reply from a case summary. In that call Claude sometimes calls lookup_order again, which adds delay and a second, different answer. The tools are still passed in the request. What is the right fix?

options.text: Set tool_choice to auto for the reply call.
