Wrap each document in XML document tags with source metadata so the model can tie each fact to its origin.

questions.question: A team extracts contract terms with tool use and a JSON schema, and parsing failures are gone. Some extractions put the effective date after the termination date, or swap the customer and vendor names. What should the team add?

options.text: Semantic validation in code, such as checking that the effective date comes before the termination date, with a retry that includes the errors.
Run every extraction twice and accept a result only when both runs return the same values.
Strict regex date patterns on every date field and enum constraints on each party role field.
Force the extraction tool with tool_choice on every request so the schema applies to each contract.

questions.question: A CI review job uses a report_findings tool with tool_choice “auto” and parses response.content[0] as the findings. Runs fail when a text block comes first. The text summary must still appear in the PR comment. How should extraction be fixed?

options.text: Set strict: true on the tool definition so the tool_use block is always the first content block.
Add a prompt rule that forbids any text before the tool call and keep parsing response.content[0].
Force tool_choice to report_findings so the response starts with the tool call.
Select the content block whose type is tool_use and read the findings from its input field.

questions.question: Developers dismiss about 40% of a reviewer’s posted findings with one click and rarely say why. You want to learn which code constructs trigger the dismissed findings without adding work for developers. What should you change?

options.text: Add a detected_pattern field to each finding’s schema that records the construct that triggered it.
Route each finding through a second independent Claude instance before it is posted.
Add few-shot examples to the review prompt that contrast dismissed findings with real issues.
Require developers to pick a dismissal reason from a fixed list each time they close a finding.

questions.question: A team wrote a brand-new audit prompt and plans one Message Batches API run across 12,000 source files. They want to avoid paying for repeated large runs. What should they do before submitting?

options.text: Define the audit output as a tool with a strict JSON schema so malformed responses can’t happen.
Submit the full batch now, then use custom_id to find failures and resubmit only those with a corrected prompt.
Run the prompt synchronously on a representative sample of files, refine it, then submit the full batch.
Split the files into several smaller batches and review each batch’s results before submitting the next.

questions.question: A review findings schema uses a category enum: bug, security, performance, style. Merge gates route each finding by its category. Reviews keep producing issue types that fit no category, so the model forces the closest match. Which schema change handles this best?

options.text: Add an “other” value to the category enum, paired with a string field describing the issue.
Make the category field optional so the model can leave it out when nothing fits.
Add a new enum value to the schema each time an uncategorized issue type appears.
Replace the enum with a free-text string so the model can name any category.

questions.question: An automated reviewer posts findings in two categories, security and correctness, each above 90% precision, and developers act on almost every finding. The team wants to add an untested deprecated-API category. The PR interface shows every finding the same way, with no labels or confidence and no way to filter categories. How should the team introduce it?

options.text: Enable it in production now but label its findings experimental so developers judge them separately.
Add “only report high-confidence deprecations” to its prompt, then enable it with the others.
Run the new category offline on recent merged pull requests, measure its false-positive rate and enable it only once precision is acceptable.
Enable it in production with a self-rated confidence on each finding so developers can skip low ones.

questions.question: Before the first nightly batch, a team will refine its test-generation prompt on a sample, scoring many prompt versions a day. The sample scores must predict full-run quality. Which two practices are correct? (select two)

options.text: Have a senior engineer hand-grade every sample output in each round before the next version.
Score each round with automated checks, such as code-based validation of the generated tests.
Choose sample pull requests that mirror the real mix of change types and include known edge cases.
Build the sample only from pull requests where earlier versions produced duplicate or wrong tests.

questions.question: A review step defines a report_findings tool with an input_schema. Claude calls it every run, but the input sometimes gives severity as the string “2” instead of the integer 2, or leaves out a required field, and the parser fails. Which change guarantees the tool input matches the schema?

options.text: Set tool_choice to {“type”: “tool”, “name”: “report_findings”} to force the call.
Add input_examples to the tool definition showing correctly typed findings.
Validate each input in code and retry with the type errors included.
Add “strict”: true to the report_findings tool definition.

questions.question: A nightly Message Batches job generates test cases with one request per changed file. Results arrive out of submission order, and some requests fail with errors instead of output. How should the pipeline link each result to its source file?

options.text: Match each result line to the request at the same position in the submitted array.
Have the model include the source file path in its JSON output and match on that.
Give each request a unique custom_id that identifies its file, and read that ID from each result line.
Poll the batch endpoint with each custom_id to fetch that request’s status and output one by one.

questions.question: A team added four few-shot examples to its review prompt, each flagging a hardcoded value. Findings are now consistently formatted, but the reviewer also flags named constants that the prose rules explicitly allow. What revision is most effective?

options.text: Replace two examples with allowed hardcoded values, each with a short reason it isn’t flagged.
Remove the examples and rely on the prose rules alone.
Move the prose exemptions to the top of the prompt and mark them IMPORTANT.
Add four more examples flagging other kinds of hardcoded values.

questions.question: A weekly dependency-license audit runs on the Message Batches API for its 50% saving, and compliance needs the report within 30 hours of each code freeze. How should the team schedule the batch?

options.text: Move the audit to the synchronous Messages API so completion time is predictable.
Submit at any point in the 30-hour window, since most batches finish within an hour.
Cancel and resubmit the batch if it hasn’t finished within an hour of submission.
Submit the audit batch no later than 6 hours after the code freeze.

questions.question: A job extracts dependency updates from PR descriptions using a tool’s JSON schema, and each prompt already includes the PR’s creation date and timezone. Extractions validate, but dates and versions keep their source formats, including relative dates like “last Tuesday”. New styles appear weekly, and deduplication needs a canonical format. What should you change?

options.text: Add stricter string constraints, such as length limits, so non-canonical values are rejected.
Add a post-processing step that rewrites dates and versions into canonical form with regular expressions.
Add normalization rules to the prompt: dates as ISO 8601 (YYYY-MM-DD) and versions as MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH without prefixes.
Add few-shot examples covering every date and version style the team has seen.

questions.question: A release-notes pipeline extracts entries from each merged PR with a validation-retry loop. Date format errors clear after one retry, but ticket_summary fails every retry because the ticket text exists only in the issue tracker, not in the diff. Release notes must include ticket summaries. What should you change?

options.text: Fetch the linked ticket text from the issue tracker and add it to the extraction context.
Make ticket_summary nullable so a retry can return null when the diff lacks the text.
Raise the retry limit and include the diff, the failed extraction and the errors in each retry.
Define the extraction as a tool with a JSON schema so ticket_summary always arrives valid.

questions.question: A nightly test-generation batch defines a client-executed read_fixtures tool in each request. When you retrieve the results, many requests succeeded but ended with stop_reason tool_use and contain tool_use blocks instead of finished suggestions. How should the pipeline handle them?

options.text: Remove read_fixtures from every request and resubmit the batch without tool use.
Keep polling the batch until the worker runs the tool and final suggestions appear.
Run each requested tool, then send a follow-up request containing the assistant content and the tool_result.
Match these results by custom_id and resubmit the identical requests in a new batch.

questions.question: A review prompt tells Claude to “flag an issue only when you are certain it is real.” Findings already follow the required format, but harmless comment wording is still reported as a bug, and the same code is flagged in some runs and not others. Which change improves precision most?

options.text: Run each review twice and report only findings that appear in both runs.
Add few-shot examples showing the required format: location, issue, severity and fix.
Have the model attach a confidence score to each finding and filter out those below 0.8.
Replace the certainty instruction with named rules for which comment issues to flag and which to skip.

questions.question: Extractions from a system always pass JSON Schema validation, but buyer and seller names sometimes end up in each other’s fields. A self-review instruction in the extraction prompt rarely changes anything. Which design catches these subtle errors best?

options.text: Enable extended thinking for the extraction so the model deliberates longer.
Add a retry loop that sends JSON Schema errors back with the document for correction.
Send the document and the finished extraction to a second Claude instance with no prior context for verification.
Send a follow-up in the same conversation asking Claude to re-check for swapped fields.

questions.question: A pipeline runs document extraction on a model that supports both forced tool use and manual extended thinking. To improve accuracy, the team enables thinking: {“type”: “enabled”, “budget_tokens”: 10000} on requests that force tool_choice {“type”: “tool”, “name”: “extract_metadata”}. Every request now fails, and each document must still produce a structured extraction through a tool call. What should change?

options.text: Change tool_choice to {“type”: “auto”} and tell the prompt to always call extract_metadata.
Keep both settings and retry the failed requests with exponential backoff.
Remove the thinking parameter from these extraction requests and keep the forced tool_choice.
Change tool_choice to {“type”: “any”} so thinking can stay on.

questions.question: A system extracts fields from 12-document loan packets in one pass over the whole packet. Some documents come back complete, others shallow or incomplete, and conflicting borrower addresses across documents go unflagged. How should the extraction be restructured?

options.text: Keep the single pass and add few-shot examples showing complete extraction for every document type.
Move to a model with a larger context window so one pass can attend to all twelve documents.
Extract each document in its own pass, then run a separate pass that compares values across documents and flags conflicts.
Run three extractions of the full packet and keep only values that at least two runs agree on.

questions.question: An extraction schema’s category enum includes “Unclear” for ambiguous documents. The schema is shared with downstream systems and must not change. In a nightly batch, some correct classifications come back as “unclear” and fail validation, and retries with the error sometimes return the same lowercase value. What is the right fix?

options.text: Raise the retry budget until a correctly capitalized value comes back.
Rewrite every enum value in lowercase so the output matches.
Compare the returned category with the enum values case-insensitively in the validation step.
Add a prompt instruction requiring the exact capitalization from the schema.

questions.question: A pipeline extracts ticket_id from each PR description. The schema allows null and the prompt says to return null when no ticket is referenced, but all three few-shot examples show a ticket. On PRs without a ticket, the model invents a plausible ID that passes validation. What addresses the fabrication most directly?

options.text: Define the extraction as a tool with the ticket schema and read ticket_id from the tool_use block.
Add a few-shot example where the description has no ticket and the output sets ticket_id to null.
Repeat the null rule at the end of the prompt and mark it IMPORTANT.
Add more examples with varied real ticket ID formats.

questions.question: A nightly extraction pulls stated_total from each test log’s summary line, calculated_total from the per-suite counts, and a conflict_detected flag. Several runs set the flag, and spot checks show the extraction is faithful: the log itself is inconsistent because of a reporter bug. How should the pipeline handle these runs?

options.text: Tell Claude to reconcile the two counts and report one consistent total.
Retry with the failed output and the two totals included as error feedback.
Route runs with conflict_detected set to a separate review path instead of re-extracting.
Replace stated_total with calculated_total before the summary reaches dashboards.

questions.question: A findings schema marks affected_test_file as a required string naming the test that covers the flagged code. Some changed modules have no tests yet, and Claude fills the field with plausible paths to nonexistent files, which PR comments then link to. Which change prevents the fabricated paths?

options.text: Check each path against the repository and retry with the validation error.
Add a prompt instruction to name only test files that exist.
Add few-shot examples contrasting findings from tested and untested modules.
Allow null for affected_test_file and remove it from the schema’s required list.

questions.question: A nightly test-generation batch for 3,000 files ends with 150 errored results. Most show invalid_request_error with “prompt is too long”; the rest are server errors. What is the correct resubmission workflow?

options.text: Find the failed files by custom_id and resubmit all of them unchanged in a new batch.
Send the oversized files unchanged through the synchronous Messages API.
Resubmit only the failed requests with a higher max_tokens on each so longer inputs fit.
Find the failed files by custom_id, chunk the oversized ones and resubmit only those requests in a new batch.

questions.question: A findings schema already records detected_pattern. A month of dismissal data shows one construct causes 70% of dismissals: guard clauses with early returns, flagged as missing error handling. Other correctness findings are rarely dismissed and catch real bugs. What is the most effective fix?

options.text: Disable the correctness category and re-enable it after its prompts are rewritten and tested.
Add a general instruction to be more conservative and report only high-confidence findings.
Add an explicit rule that guard clauses with early returns aren’t reportable as missing error handling.
Add a self-reported confidence score to every finding so developers can triage.

questions.question: A review step outputs findings as JSON that your code validates with Pydantic. One run is rejected because two findings cite line numbers that don’t exist in the PR diff. How should you build the retry?

options.text: Turn the two rejected findings into contrastive examples and re-run the whole review.
Send the PR diff, the rejected findings and the exact validation errors, and ask for a corrected output.
Send only the rejected findings with the errors, and ask the model to fix the line numbers.
Send the rejected findings, the errors and only the diff hunks those findings cite.

questions.question: After sample refinement met the quality target, an engineer restructured each batch request to add a tool definition for structured findings. The nightly batch then ended with every request errored for invalid params. What should the team do before resubmitting?

options.text: Repeat the sample refinement loop to raise first-pass quality.
Add strict: true to the tool definition so the API enforces the schema.
Split the corpus into smaller batches so a failure affects fewer requests.
Send a few of the restructured requests through the synchronous Messages API before submitting the full batch.

questions.question: An automated review emits each finding through tool use with an input_schema. Every finding parses and severity is always a valid enum value, but developers report that minor issues are often labeled critical. What addresses this?

options.text: Add explicit severity criteria to the review prompt, with an example issue for each level.
Enable strict mode (strict: true) on the findings tool.
Add a retry step that resends each finding with its schema errors.
Set the sampling temperature to zero.

questions.question: On contracts longer than 20,000 tokens, the model invents clause details that the source contradicts, while shorter documents extract accurately. More few-shot examples didn’t change the error rate. Which change reduces these fabrications most directly?

options.text: Rebuild the example set with ten examples from full-length production contracts.
Make every clause field nullable so the model can return null.
Set the sampling temperature to zero.
Ask the model to extract word-for-word quotes for each field first, then fill the schema from those quotes.

questions.question: Invoices contain an order date, a ship date and a due date. The extraction prompt says only “extract the invoice date.” Extractions pass validation, but different runs put a different one of these dates in invoice_date for the same invoice. Which change fixes this most reliably?

options.text: Add a rule naming the exact label that maps to invoice_date, plus a fallback for invoices without that label.
Add a validation-retry loop that sends schema errors back for correction.
Have a second Claude instance review each extraction and replace any wrong date.
Add three few-shot examples showing the exact JSON structure to return.

questions.question: An extraction schema has stated_total, calculated_total and a conflict_detected boolean. An audit finds records where the two totals differ but conflict_detected is false. Downstream systems filter on this flag alone and must never receive a wrong flag. What is the right fix?

options.text: Retry with a prompt that quotes the two totals and the wrong flag value.
Add few-shot examples that set the flag whenever the two totals differ.
Make conflict_detected a required, strictly typed boolean in the schema.
Compare the two totals in validation code after each extraction and overwrite conflict_detected with the result.

questions.question: Extractions from a tool_use pipeline always pass validation, but the same information lands in different fields across documents with inline citations, narrative text and tables. Detailed instructions haven’t fixed this. Which two changes address the inconsistency best? (select two)

options.text: Enable strict tool use with strict: true so inputs are validated against the schema.
Wrap each example in dedicated example XML tags so the model can tell examples from instructions.
Retry each inconsistent extraction with the previous output and the validation error.
Add 3 to 5 examples drawn from the real document structures, covering each structure type.

questions.question: A review step defines three finding tools, one per issue category, and the right category varies per pull request. tool_choice is {“type”: “any”} on a model that supports forced tool use. Some responses contain two tool_use blocks, and some tool inputs miss a required field. The parser needs exactly one schema-conformant tool call per response. Which two changes fix these problems? (select two)

options.text: Add disable_parallel_tool_use: true inside the tool_choice object.
Add a system prompt rule that Claude must call one tool and fill every required field.
Set strict: true on each of the three tool definitions.
Change tool_choice to force one named finding tool on every review.

questions.question: A review step reports a per-PR summary through a tool call. One integer field counts affected API endpoints, which means tracing calls across several files. Every response matches the schema, but the count is often wrong, and cost rules allow one model call per PR. What improves the count’s accuracy?

options.text: Tell Claude to trace and count the affected endpoints in text before it makes the tool call.
Run a second independent Claude instance to re-derive the count and flag disagreements.
Set strict: true on the tool definition.
Add minimum and maximum bounds to the count field.

questions.question: An extraction schema’s category enum includes “unclear” for ambiguous documents. Every extraction passes validation, but the model almost never returns “unclear” and assigns a best-fit label even to documents reviewers judge genuinely ambiguous. What fixes this most directly?

options.text: Add a validation retry that resends the document with the errors from the failed extraction.
Make the category field nullable so the model can return null.
Set strict: true on the extraction tool.
Describe when to choose “unclear” in the field description and the prompt, giving the model explicit permission to be uncertain.

questions.question: Reviewers now dismiss an extraction system’s flags unread, including flags that catch real total mismatches. The dashboard shows 85% overall flag precision, and the team can’t agree which flag type is to blame. What should you do first?

options.text: Attach a self-rated confidence score to every flag.
Tighten the criteria uniformly across all categories.
Label a recent sample of flags and measure precision separately for each flag category.
Add few-shot examples of correct flags and non-flags for every category.

questions.question: A contract extraction pipeline defines an extraction tool whose input_schema is the output format, with strict: true. The team is trimming its validation code. Which two checks must stay? (select two)

options.text: A check that each extracted party name appears in the source document text.
A repair step that fixes unclosed braces and trailing commas before parsing.
A check that flags extractions where end_date is earlier than start_date.
A check that every required field is present with the schema’s declared type.

questions.question: A nightly Message Batch extracts data from thousands of documents, each identified by a file path that contains slashes. Which two design choices map each result back to its source document correctly? (select two)

options.text: Poll the batch by its Message Batch ID, then match each .jsonl result line to its document by custom_id.
Convert each file path into an ID using only letters, digits, hyphens and underscores, and use it as the custom_id.
Read the .jsonl results in order and match each line by its position in the submitted array.
Use each document’s raw file path as its custom_id and look results up by path.

questions.question: An extraction tool runs with strict tool use, so its inputs always match the schema’s types and required fields. Downstream systems also need a non-negative amount and a nine-character tax_id. Which approach guarantees these two rules?

options.text: State the range and length rules as normalization instructions in the system prompt.
Add few-shot examples with a non-negative amount and a nine-character tax_id.
Keep the strict schema as is and check the range and length rules in code after parsing.
Add minimum to amount and minLength and maxLength to tax_id in the strict input_schema.

questions.question: A support agent tags every issue a message raises, for routing. The prompt has three single-issue few-shot examples. Formatting is now consistent, but when a customer reports a late delivery and a double charge together, only the first issue is tagged. What fixes this?

options.text: Remove the examples and describe the tagging rules in prose, keeping the format instructions.
Add a sentence saying some messages raise several issues and each needs its own tag.
Replace them with varied examples, including messages with two or three issues that are each fully tagged.
Add examples of the other issue types, showing the full set of tags the model may use.

questions.question: A support agent records a refund amount from phrases like “$12”, “12 bucks” and “twelve fifty” before calling process_refund. The API requires whole-number cents, but the record holds a string. Which change makes the handoff reliable?

options.text: Normalize the phrase in application code, reject ambiguous amounts, and validate an integer cents field before calling process_refund.
Change the record to integer cents and let Claude interpret each phrase with its own judgment.
Keep a string field with a dollar regex and rely on strict mode to convert matching values to cents.
Keep the string and teach process_refund to parse spoken amounts while keeping its current contract.

questions.question: Three independent reviewer instances check each refactor, and a finding is posted only when two report it. An audit of last month’s discarded single-reviewer findings turned up a SQL injection, a race condition and a data-loss bug. What change fits best?

options.text: Post single-reviewer findings only in the security category and keep two-of-three for the rest.
Add a fourth reviewer and keep the majority rule.
Post every finding any reviewer reports, labeled with how many of the three flagged it.
Keep two-of-three and give the reviewers a shared checklist to raise agreement.

questions.question: In one Claude Code session, Claude writes a patch and then declares it correct. The team wants a cheap check in the same session before an independent review runs later, and test and lint commands exist. What is most useful?

options.text: Ask Claude to check the diff against the acceptance criteria and list any unmet requirement.
Run the relevant tests and lint in the same session and report their actual output with the list of changed files.
Ask Claude to rate its confidence in each changed file and flag any below 7.
Ask for a second, more skeptical written critique of the patch.

questions.question: A test-writing job creates tests from the changed code, and a second Claude instance reviews them by reading the same code. Both approved a pull request with wrong discount rounding: the tests assert exactly what the code does. What should the reviewer check the tests against?

options.text: Property-based tests generated from the changed code.
The changed code again, with a checklist of common rounding mistakes.
A mutation test run that rejects tests that miss code changes.
The ticket’s acceptance criteria, confirming each rule has a test that checks its stated result.

questions.question: A separate verifier instance checks each research report before release but receives only the report text. Spot checks find approved reports whose cited sources don’t say what the report claims. Which two changes make the verifier effective? (select two)

options.text: Run three verifiers on the report text and release only when two approve.
Give the verifier the cited excerpt for each claim, placed right next to that claim.
Have the writing subagent re-check its own citations in the same session.
Ask for a verdict on each claim, supported or not supported, quoting the exact source line it relied on.

questions.question: A reviewer posts several “critical” findings a week, such as possible null dereferences. About half turn out to be wrong, and developers now argue with every critical label. What should the team require?

options.text: A confidence score, posting critical findings only above 0.8.
A second reviewer, posting critical findings only when both report them.
A failing test or command output attached to each critical finding, showing the problem actually occurs.
A lower severity label for every finding.

questions.question: Many review comments land on files nobody edits by hand, and on spacing problems another CI step already fails the build for. Developers now dismiss whole reviews unread. What change to the review prompt fits best?

options.text: Report only findings the reviewer is highly confident about.
Cap each review at ten comments ordered by severity.
Comment only on changed lines and ignore everything else.
List what not to review: generated code, lockfiles and anything existing CI checks already enforce.

questions.question: A team keeps Message Batches results in the API and downloads each month’s results for audit at month end. Results for a batch created 35 days earlier could not be downloaded. What should change?

options.text: Download from the results URL saved when the batch was created.
Download and store each batch’s results when it ends, within the 29 days the API keeps them.
Resubmit the batch to regenerate its results before the audit.
Set a longer results retention period when creating each batch.

questions.question: After a new schema version was deployed, every extraction request fails with a 400 invalid_request_error pointing at an unsupported schema keyword. The retry logic retries each request five times with backoff, and the queue is backing up. What should change?

options.text: Switch to plain prompting with the schema in the prompt to keep the queue moving.
Stop retrying these errors right away, alert the team and fix the schema.
Keep retrying but cap retries at two per request.
Send failures to a dead-letter queue and retry them hourly until the fix ships.

questions.question: A Message Batch of 10,000 extraction requests has ended: 9,812 succeeded, 150 errored and 38 expired. Results come back in a different order from submission. What should the job do next?

options.text: Resubmit the 188 failed requests in their original order.
Match results by custom_id and resubmit the errored and expired requests.
Match results by custom_id and resubmit only the errored requests.
Match results by line number and resubmit the errored and expired rows.

questions.question: Some scans fail extraction again and again because pages are unreadable, and the retry loop keeps resending the same document, so the job never finishes. Which two controls make recovery safe? (select two)

options.text: Retry with backoff and sharper scan rendering until one response passes validation.
Limit each document to three logged extraction attempts, stopping automatic retries when the budget is used up.
Send unresolved documents to human review with the scan, earlier outputs and each attempt’s validation errors.
After three failures, mark the job complete and drop the document without review.

questions.question: A team moves extraction to the Message Batches API. To save tokens, only the first request carries the long field definitions; the other 4,999 say “Apply the same instructions to this document,” and most of those results are poor. What explains this, and what is the fix?

options.text: Batch requests share one system prompt; put the definitions once in a batch-level system field.
Each request is processed independently; include the complete definitions in each one and use prompt caching to cut the cost.
Batches discard system prompts; move the definitions into the first request’s user message.
Requests share a cache, not a conversation; set cache_control on the first request so others reuse it.

questions.question: When an invoice has no tax ID, the extractor can call lookup_vendor_tax_id or mark the field absent. The rule: look it up for registered companies, mark it absent for private sellers. Claude switches between the two paths at random. Which prompt change helps most?

options.text: Add one example per seller type showing the source excerpt, its lookup_vendor_tax_id call (if any) and the final JSON.
Add completed JSON examples for both seller types without the tool calls.
Say “use when needed” in the tool description and let Claude decide.
Force lookup_vendor_tax_id on every invoice and discard the result for private sellers.

questions.question: A report writer says a new clinic cut emergency visits by 20%. A reviewer subagent marks it unsupported, and the writer points to a passage that may support a narrower claim. The statement will shape a funding vote. What should the coordinator do?

options.text: Keep the writer’s version once a person confirms the passage exists.
Run a third reviewer and publish whichever reading two of three support.
Escalate the claim, the passage and both reviews to a human analyst for a final ruling.
Publish the narrower claim and note that the reviewer disputed the 20% figure.

questions.question: Two reviewer subagents check each weekly report with the same instruction, “review for quality.” Their comments overlap while real problems go unnoticed. One is strong at source provenance, the other at spotting claims that go beyond the evidence. How should they be set up?

options.text: Give one a provenance checklist (source exists, publication date, primary or secondary) and the other a claim-strength checklist, then merge their findings.
Have the second reviewer read the first one’s comments and focus where the first raised doubts.
Give both the same full checklist and keep only findings both report.
Have both score each section from 1 to 5 and escalate sections with the biggest gap.

questions.question: A research document subagent analyzes each of 30 sources in its own pass, then runs a final integration pass over all 30 full texts again. That pass often hits the context limit and repeats per-source findings instead of comparing sources. What should the integration pass receive and do?

options.text: All 30 full texts again in three batches of ten, summarizing each batch separately.
The same 30 full texts, with instructions to skip findings already reported.
Only the per-source findings, with instructions to find cross-source issues such as contradictions, duplicates and coverage gaps.
Only the per-source findings, with instructions to rank them and merge them into one list.

questions.question: A verification subagent marks every claim in a report pass or fail, and editors get about 200 failures a week. Most are minor wording issues, but a few are unsupported figures that must never ship. How should the verification output change?

options.text: Report only failures the subagent considers important and drop minor ones.
Attach a severity and a confidence score to each failure, sending unsupported figures straight to editors and batching wording issues.
Keep pass or fail and have a second subagent re-check every failure first.
Replace per-claim results with one quality score per report.

questions.question: A test-generation job validates its JSON output. Four failures recur: owner is empty because the repository has no CODEOWNERS entry; test paths use backslashes; ticket_id is empty because the PR names no ticket; coverage_delta doesn’t match the numbers in the prompt. Which two would a retry with the error attached likely fix? (select two)

options.text: The empty owner, where no CODEOWNERS entry covers the changed files.
The empty ticket_id, where the description names no ticket.
The test paths written with backslashes instead of the forward slashes the schema requires.
The coverage_delta that doesn’t match the before and after figures in the prompt.

questions.question: A review prompt says: “Do not comment on logging.” Claude now skips missing audit logs in payment code, which security requires, and ignores log lines that expose card numbers. Which two prompt changes fit? (select two)

options.text: Explain the reason: logging style is already enforced by a linter, so style comments only add noise.
Repeat the instruction in capitals at the start and end of the prompt.
State the exceptions: always report logging that exposes sensitive customer data or misses a required audit event.
Remove the instruction and let Claude comment on any logging issue.

questions.question: A CI step sends Claude one report per run, with one extraction tool each for JUnit, coverage and lint reports. On a model that supports forced tool use, the request forces the JUnit extractor, so coverage and lint reports come back empty. Most file names reveal the type accurately; some reveal nothing. What should the request set?

options.text: tool_choice any every time, plus a retry when the tool doesn’t match the file name.
tool_choice any every time, with the file name in the prompt as a hint.
Force the extractor the file name suggests, and the JUnit extractor when the name is unclear.
Force the matching extractor when the file name identifies the report, and any when it doesn’t.

questions.question: A review job’s JSON schema requires at least one item in findings. For clean pull requests, Claude sometimes invents a minor finding and sometimes replies in prose, which breaks the parser. What should change?

options.text: Keep the schema and retry prose replies, asking for JSON.
Allow an empty findings array so a clean pull request returns valid JSON with no invented findings.
Keep the minimum and have the parser drop findings labeled minor.
Keep the schema and add an example where the single finding says no issues were found.

questions.question: To stop invented values, a team made termination_date optional in its contract schema. Fabrication stopped, but the downstream loader now crashes on records where the key is missing entirely. What should the schema do?

options.text: Keep it optional and tell Claude to always include the key, set to null when absent.
Make termination_date required with a type of date string or null, so the key is always present.
Make it required as date string or null, defaulting to the signing date when the contract is silent.
Keep it optional and have the loader skip records without the key.

questions.question: Midway through a research task, the requester writes: “A human analyst must take over now. Run no more searches and generate no new analysis.” Two planned searches would complete the topic, and the findings so far are stored as structured claim-source records. What should the coordinator do?

options.text: Pause the searches, but have the synthesis agent write a summary of existing findings before the transfer.
Transfer the task to a human analyst now, passing along the structured findings already collected.
Transfer now, but queue the two remaining searches so their results reach the analyst later.
Finish the two remaining searches first so the analyst receives a complete handoff package.

questions.question: A research coordinator’s system prompt says only “escalate to the operator when uncertain.” In testing it escalates transient search failures that a retry would fix, and it silently picks one reading of ambiguous requests instead of asking. Which change fixes both behaviors most effectively?

options.text: Add a hook on escalate_to_operator calls that blocks escalations whose reason is a transient search failure.
Deploy a separate classifier model, trained on past runs, to decide which requests need the operator.
Add explicit escalation criteria to the system prompt with few-shot examples of cases to escalate and cases to handle autonomously.
Have the coordinator rate its confidence from 1 to 10 before each decision and escalate below a threshold.

questions.question: A team’s triage assistant handles build-failure reports and can escalate to an on-call engineer. A developer writes: “This test broke my branch again, this is absurd.” The fix is routine and within the assistant’s scope. How should it respond?

options.text: Escalate to the on-call engineer with a structured handoff that includes the failure details and the message.
Score the message’s sentiment and escalate when frustration crosses a set threshold.
Acknowledge the frustration, apply the routine fix, and escalate only if the developer then asks for a human.
Acknowledge the frustration, then ask whether the developer wants the assistant’s fix or an on-call engineer first.

questions.question: A CI review prompt asks Claude to attach a self-reported confidence value to each finding, and findings above 0.9 skip human review. Error rates within those skipped findings must stay measured per rule family as the codebase changes. Which design meets this need?

options.text: Each month, have humans review a random sample of skipped findings drawn from every rule family.
Each month, re-run the calibration checks on the labeled validation set and adjust the 0.9 threshold.
Each month, run a second independent Claude instance over the skipped findings and track disagreement per rule family.
Each month, have humans review every finding Claude marked low confidence, grouped by rule family.

questions.question: A weekly report slash command outputs benchmark timings, an incident account and flagged code issues, all as bullet points. Reviewers can’t compare benchmarks across weeks, and the incident reads as fragments instead of a chronological story. Which prompt change fixes both complaints?

options.text: Add few-shot examples of past bullet-point reports so the format stays consistent each week.
Have the command render the benchmarks as a table, the incident as prose and the flagged issues as a structured list.
Use one section template that renders the benchmarks as a table and every other section as a structured list.
Switch the whole report to flowing prose so each section connects to the next.

questions.question: During an unattended nightly audit, an analysis subagent finds that the vendor changelog and the team’s benchmark report give different latency figures for the same library release. The main session drafts the final report after all subagents finish. What should the subagent return?

options.text: Only the figure from the more recently published source, noting that the older one was superseded.
One consolidated figure computed as the midpoint of the two values.
Pause mid-analysis and ask the developer which source to trust before continuing.
Both figures with their sources, flagged as a conflict, so the main session can reconcile them before drafting.

questions.question: Some documents report two credible figures for the same metric, from studies with different dates and methods. The output schema holds one value per field, so one figure is silently dropped. Analysts downstream need both figures with their source context. What is the best fix?

options.text: Tell the model to extract the figure from the most recent study and ignore older values.
Change the schema so a metric holds a list of values, each with source name, date and method, plus a conflict flag.
Add a validation retry that re-sends the document with the flagged field so the model corrects the value.
Add a field-level confidence score and send documents with two candidate values to human review for a final choice.

questions.question: Downstream systems flag many extracted market-size figures as contradictory. An audit shows the differing values are all accurate: the source documents cover different reporting periods. Which change to the extraction system prevents this misinterpretation?

options.text: Send both extractions back to the model with a validation error so it corrects the disagreement.
Keep only one value per metric, using the figure from the document judged most recent.
Mark each pair of differing values as a conflict with source attribution and send it to a human reviewer.
Add a publication or data-collection date field to the extraction schema, nullable when the document gives none.

questions.question: A parsing step in an extraction pipeline reports every failure as a generic ’extraction failed’ status, whether the PDF was corrupted or the request timed out. What should the parsing component return so the coordinator can decide whether to retry, split the document or skip it?

options.text: The failure type, any pages already extracted as partial results, and suggested alternative approaches.
Nothing until it has retried transient failures internally with exponential backoff; only persistent failures reach the coordinator.
The full raw parser logs attached to each error so the coordinator has complete diagnostic detail.
A success status with null extraction fields so downstream validation flags the document later.

questions.question: During a debugging session, a developer tells Claude Code: “Find out why this test fails, but don’t change any files; I’ll make the fix myself.” Claude finds the cause, a one-character typo. What is the correct behavior?

options.text: Ask the developer whether the no-edit instruction still applies to a fix this small.
Report the root cause and show the suggested change as text, leaving every file untouched.
Enter plan mode, present the edit as a plan, and apply it after the developer approves.
Apply the one-line fix and show the diff so the developer can review it afterward.

questions.question: A Claude Code session writes a pre-refactor assessment of a legacy module. The report states reproduced test failures and hedged guesses from old code comments with the same certainty. Uncertain items must stay visible so the team can investigate them. Which change fixes this?

options.text: Send the draft to a second independent Claude instance to verify each finding.
Add a self-critique pass where the agent removes any claim it can’t verify against the code.
Tell the agent to attach a confidence score from 1 to 10 to every finding.
Define report sections that separate verified findings from unconfirmed claims, keeping each source’s original wording.

questions.question: Claude Code runs refactoring tasks autonomously after an engineer approves each plan in plan mode, and every change also goes through pull request review. Which two rules should trigger a mid-task handoff to an engineer? (select two)

options.text: Hand off when CLAUDE.md and the team’s conventions give no guidance on a design decision the task requires.
Hand off whenever Claude reports a self-rated confidence below the team’s autonomy threshold.
Hand off when repeated fix attempts leave the same test failing and each attempt adds no new information.
Hand off whenever the refactor turns out to touch more than ten files across several modules.

questions.question: Senior engineers labeled 400 of Claude’s pull request reviews, including reviews that found no issues, across several languages and finding categories. Overall accuracy is 96%, and leadership wants to end mandatory human review. What should you check first?

options.text: Compare the 96% with the measured accuracy of human reviewers and proceed if Claude scores higher.
Have Claude rate its confidence on each review and skip human review above a threshold.
Break the 96% down by language and finding category and confirm that every segment performs consistently.
Grow the labeled set to 2,000 reviews to narrow the margin of error on the overall figure.

questions.question: In production, a support agent’s lookup_order fails for three reasons: backend timeouts, badly formatted order numbers and order IDs that don’t exist. The MCP server returns “lookup failed” for all three, so the agent escalates almost every failure. What change enables correct recovery?

options.text: Map all three failures to one customer-facing message that the agent relays word for word.
Return an error category (transient, validation, not_found), an isRetryable flag and a suggested next step in each tool error.
Tell the agent in the system prompt to retry a failed lookup once, then ask the customer to re-enter the number.
Add retries with exponential backoff inside the MCP server and return failures only after they’re exhausted.

questions.question: A customer asks a support agent to match a competitor’s lower advertised price. The pricing policy covers only adjustments for items discounted on the company’s own site and says nothing about competitor prices. How should the agent handle this?

options.text: Call escalate_to_human and hand the request to a person for review.
Decline, telling the customer the policy doesn’t allow competitor price matching.
Ask the customer for proof of the competitor’s price before deciding.
Offer the own-site price adjustment amount by applying the closest policy rule.

questions.question: A long Claude Code session debugging an agent’s escalation logic is nearly out of context because of verbose discovery output. The developer must free context now, keep the refund-threshold findings and continue the same investigation. What should they do?

options.text: Delegate the rest of the investigation to a subagent so new output stays out of the main context.
Run /clear to reset the context, then restate the goal in a fresh conversation.
Run /autocompact with a lower token threshold so compaction happens sooner.
Run /compact with focus instructions telling the summary to keep the refund-threshold findings.

questions.question: An extraction assistant can route cases to a human reviewer. A user reports a wrong invoice total, and the assistant offers a corrected re-extraction that would likely fix it. The user replies: “No, have a person check it.” What should the assistant do?

options.text: Acknowledge the frustration again and offer a side-by-side view of extracted and source values.
Escalate only if the message scores above a frustration threshold in sentiment analysis.
Run the re-extraction first, then escalate with the new result if the user is still unhappy.
Route the case to the human reviewer now, without running the re-extraction.

questions.question: A synthesis report lists extracted revenue figures in the order the source documents were processed. Each figure carries its reporting period and source. Analysts compare exact quarterly values and say they can’t follow the trend. Which output change fixes this?

options.text: Group the figures under a heading for each source document so provenance stays visible.
Turn the whole report into one uniform table so every section renders the same way.
Order the revenue figures chronologically by reporting period.
Rewrite the figures as prose describing the overall trend.

questions.question: A system outputs one confidence score per document, and documents above 0.85 skip human review. Reviewers, whose capacity is fixed, still find frequent date-field errors in documents above 0.85. Which change improves review routing?

options.text: Raise the document-level threshold from 0.85 to 0.95 so more borderline documents get reviewed.
Output a confidence score per field and calibrate each field’s review threshold on a labeled validation set.
Tell the model to report lower confidence when a field’s source text is ambiguous.
Add random sampling of documents that skip review to measure that population’s error rate.

questions.question: A research system’s web search subagent hits frequent timeouts from its external API. One quick retry fixes most of them, but a few persist. Today every timeout goes straight to the coordinator, costing extra turns and tokens. How should the subagent handle timeouts?

options.text: After a failed local retry, return one generic ‘search unavailable’ status for all remaining failures.
Retry timeouts locally with backoff, and report persistent failures to the coordinator with the attempted query and any partial results.
Report every timeout to the coordinator immediately as structured error context.
Keep retrying inside the subagent with increasing backoff until the call succeeds.

questions.question: A research coordinator’s system prompt has explicit escalation criteria and five few-shot examples, all of which end in escalation. In production it now escalates routine cases it could resolve, such as a single search timeout. What change is most effective?

options.text: Have the coordinator rate its confidence for each case and escalate only below a calibrated threshold.
Add more escalation examples covering more failure types.
Add examples of cases to resolve autonomously alongside the escalation examples.
Replace the examples with a longer, more precise numbered list of criteria.

questions.question: A developer changed a document analysis subagent’s loop to send only the latest message and tool result in each Messages API request. Sessions stay well under the context limit, but the subagent now repeats completed lookups and contradicts its earlier findings. What should change?

options.text: Resend all earlier tool_result blocks but leave out the assistant turns that requested them.
Send the full message history, including every earlier assistant turn and tool result, in each request.
Mark the earlier turns with cache_control so the API serves them from cache without resending them.
Replace the earlier turns with a model-written summary sent with the latest exchange.

questions.question: A synthesis subagent receives a 70K-token aggregated input. Its drafts cite findings from the beginning and end but skip well-supported findings from the middle. Final reports must quote exact figures from the detailed results. How should the input be restructured?

options.text: Move the research question and instructions to the top, before the subagent results.
Put a key-findings summary at the top and mark each subagent’s detailed results with clear section headings.
Split the input and call the synthesis agent once per subagent output with a running summary.
Have each subagent compress its results into a short summary before aggregation.

questions.question: A custom audit subagent reports every call to a deprecated API, but its findings leave out file paths and line numbers. The main session has to search the codebase again to locate each call, filling its context with discovery output. Which change fixes this?

options.text: Add a required report format with file path and line range fields to the subagent’s system prompt body.
List the required output fields in the subagent’s description field.
Have the main session run Grep after each delegation to attach file locations.
Narrow the subagent’s tools frontmatter to Grep and Read.

questions.question: A coordinator script spawns one Claude Code agent per module for an overnight migration across 40 modules. Three hours in, the machine crashes. Which design lets a restarted run skip modules that already finished?

options.text: Have each agent write its status and results to a state file, and have the coordinator load a manifest on restart.
Resume each agent’s named session with –resume so its context is restored.
Have each agent keep a scratchpad of key findings and read it when context degrades.
Run /compact in each session before every phase so sessions stay small.

questions.question: A find_service MCP tool returns every match for a name fragment. For “raise the payments timeout,” three actively used services match, and Claude edits the most recently deployed one, often the wrong one. What should change?

options.text: Have Claude rate its confidence in the chosen service and edit only when confidence is high.
Add few-shot examples to CLAUDE.md showing the right service for common timeout requests.
Change find_service to rank matches by relevance and return only the top one.
Add a CLAUDE.md instruction: when find_service returns several matches, list them and ask the developer to choose.

questions.question: A Claude Code audit for deprecated API usage couldn’t read some directories, but its final report lists findings and mentions no gaps. The team still wants the partial results. Which two practices fix this? (select two)

options.text: Have the agent distinguish directories with no findings from directories it couldn’t read, instead of reporting both as clean.
Remove the unreadable directories from the report so it contains only confirmed findings.
Stop the audit and return an error whenever a directory can’t be read.
Annotate the report by area, marking which directories were fully scanned and which were skipped because they couldn’t be read.

questions.question: A team sends Claude Code changes to senior review when Claude’s self-rated confidence is below 7. An audit finds regressions in complex concurrency refactors that Claude rated 9 or 10, the same scores it gives routine renames. What should the team do?

options.text: Raise the threshold so only changes rated 10 skip senior review.
Calibrate the threshold against a labeled set of past changes and their regression outcomes.
Define explicit review criteria in the prompt, with examples of changes that do and don’t need review.
Add a self-review pass where Claude re-examines each change and updates its rating.

questions.question: Validation retries fix date-format errors in one pass, but when a scan has no readable invoice number, retries never succeed and the model eventually invents one. Downstream billing needs a real invoice number. How should these documents be handled?

options.text: Raise the retry limit and include the previous extraction and the validation error each time.
Make invoice_number nullable so the model returns null instead of inventing a value.
Add few-shot examples of invoice-number extraction from varied scanned layouts.
Detect when the invoice number is missing from the source and route those documents to human review.

questions.question: After 30 or more turns of correcting extracted invoices in one session, the assistant starts using superseded statuses and wrong totals. Compaction turned exact values into loose summaries, and each re-validation result adds over 30 fields to context. Which two changes prevent these errors? (select two)

options.text: Enable structured outputs with a strict schema so every response’s IDs, amounts and statuses are validated.
Keep a persistent structured block of invoice IDs, amounts and statuses outside the summarized history and send it with every prompt.
Rewrite the compaction prompt so every amount, ID and status is kept word for word.
Trim each re-validation result to the fields the current invoice needs before it enters context.

questions.question: During multi-hour billing dispute investigations, compaction erases the agent’s earlier reasoning. It still quotes amounts and order numbers correctly, but it forgets which explanations it already ruled out and repeats the same lookups. What should change?

options.text: Re-run the backend lookups after each compaction to rebuild the lost findings.
Rewrite the compaction prompt so every ruled-out explanation is kept word for word.
Extract amounts, dates and order numbers into a persistent case-facts block sent with every prompt.
Have the agent write key findings to a scratchpad file and consult it after compaction.

questions.question: A billing dispute covers two orders. lookup_order verifies the first but times out on the second, and retries fail during a backend outage expected to last hours. The customer asks for a human. How should the agent build the handoff?

options.text: Organize it into sections: verified findings for the first order, and the unchecked second order annotated with the failure reason.
Hold the escalation and keep retrying until the second order’s data arrives.
Escalate the first order now and open a separate follow-up case for the second.
Attach the session’s complete raw tool outputs and error responses as evidence.

questions.question: A customer disputes charges on three orders. lookup_order returns full data for two, and the lookup for the third times out even after retries. The same order-system outage also blocks the human support team. How should the agent respond?

options.text: Hold the reply and keep retrying the third lookup until data comes back.
Escalate the whole case so one human resolves all three disputes together.
Resolve the two verified orders and mark the third as unresolved because its order data is unavailable.
Resolve the two verified orders and leave the third out of the reply until the system recovers.

questions.question: Billing disputes require a customer’s full transaction history, and dispute signals can appear in any line or field (descriptors, notes, adjustments), so nothing can be removed before analysis. After these lookups, later turns misquote amounts. Which design change fixes this?

options.text: Delegate the analysis to a subagent, passing it the customer ID and dispute details, and have it return a findings summary.
Add a PostToolUse hook in the main agent that trims each transaction history to relevant fields.
Summarize the conversation right after each history lookup.
Spawn an analysis subagent and have it pull the dispute details from the main agent’s history.

questions.question: A coordinator’s escalation rule says “escalate when you are not sure you can recover.” Its two few-shot examples show only the failure and the chosen action. In testing it copies the action of whichever example looks most similar, even when the failure type differs, and production will include failure types testing never produced. Which two rewrites make the guidance effective? (select two)

options.text: Show the reasoning behind the decision in each example, not just the failure and the action.
Replace the vague rule with checkable conditions, such as escalating only when a failure persists after retries.
Add one example for each failure type seen in testing so every failure matches an example.
Have the coordinator rate its confidence from 1 to 10 and escalate below a threshold.

questions.question: Every refund waits a day in a staff queue, where reviewers reject about one in ten, mostly orders that were already refunded. Leadership wants refunds up to $20 to skip review. What should decide which ones skip it?

options.text: Deterministic code checks that the order exists, the amount is within $20 and no refund was previously posted.
Deterministic code checks that the amount is within $20 and the order exists, without checking earlier refunds.
Automatic approval of every refund up to $20, with staff auditing a random tenth each week.
The agent’s own classification of the case as routine in its summary.

questions.question: A random audit of 400 resolved support cases shows 97% accuracy overall, and 12 of the audited cases were account problems. Leadership wants to end human review of account-problem cases. What should the team do first?

options.text: Draw a fresh random sample of 400 cases of all types and measure account-case accuracy within it.
End review of account problems if none of the 12 audited account cases were wrong.
Sample enough account-problem cases on their own to measure that type’s accuracy, then decide.
Keep human review only for cases that later get a complaint or are reopened.

questions.question: Every research subagent returns claims with a source and date, yet the final brief sometimes prints figures with no source, or with another report’s date. Most errors involve claims that several sources supported. Which two changes keep attribution intact? (select two)

options.text: Have the report subagent restore missing sources at the end by searching the original documents.
Require the synthesis output to map each merged claim to all of its contributing sources and their dates.
Have synthesis write merged claims in prose, followed by a bibliography of every source used.
Validate each stage’s output in code and reject any claim that reaches the next stage without its source and date.

questions.question: At 7:40 a.m., a research system can’t retrieve today’s central bank rate decision, which the brief’s lead section requires and can’t publish without. Other sections are useful on their own and due at 8 a.m., and the duty editor may approve a brief without the lead. Two minor news sources also failed. What should the coordinator do?

options.text: Hold the whole brief and escalate, releasing nothing until the rate decision is verified.
Escalate the blocked lead section to the duty editor and, if approved, release the other sections by 8 a.m. with the minor gaps noted.
Release every section by 8 a.m. with a placeholder lead, then ask the editor to approve it afterward.
Fill the lead with yesterday’s rate decision, labeled with its date, and release on time.

questions.question: A support case has an open return and a disputed charge. A billing result settles the charge, but the return is waiting for warehouse evidence that arrives later. The agent must continue without losing either status. Which two state updates are needed? (select two)

options.text: Mark the charge issue resolved with its billing evidence, and keep the overall case open for the return.
Keep one status for the whole case, waiting on warehouse, and note the charge result as free text.
Record the return’s missing evidence and next action in its own issue entry for a later turn.
Mark the whole case resolved, and reopen it when the warehouse evidence arrives.

questions.question: An enrichment agent checks each supplier’s VAT number before an import agent loads the record. When the registry times out, the enrichment agent leaves vat_verified out, and the importer treats a missing field as verified. Timed-out records must be rechecked the next day; rejected numbers go to the supplier team. What handoff change closes the gap?

options.text: Set vat_verified to false on timeout and have the importer reject records marked false.
Add a warning to the enrichment agent’s prose message and pass the record on unchanged.
Retry the registry until it responds, holding each record until the check completes.
Send an explicit verification state (verified, failed or not checked) with its reason inside the structured record.

questions.question: A coordinator passes a synthesis subagent eight source excerpts separated by dashed lines, each with its source name on the line above. Reports sometimes quote a figure from one excerpt but credit the neighboring source. What change fits best?

options.text: List the eight source names in a table after the last excerpt, in excerpt order.
Add a rule telling synthesis to take particular care with attribution.
Wrap each excerpt in its own document tags, with the source name and content in separate subtags.
Replace the dashes with blank lines and Markdown headings above each excerpt.

questions.question: A coordinator sends all collected sources to a synthesis subagent in one request. For big topics the request fails with a context-length error, and the coordinator retries with half the sources, sometimes twice. What should it do instead?

options.text: Estimate four characters per token and split when the estimate looks too high.
Count the request’s tokens before sending, and split the sources when the count passes a set budget.
Keep retrying, but drop the least-cited half of the sources each time.
Use the model with the largest context window and keep sending everything at once.

questions.question: A freight extraction system sends every document over 20 pages or in several languages to human review. Reviewers find 95% of those extractions already correct, while errors in short documents pass straight through. What should decide review?

options.text: A lower page threshold of ten pages, still sending all multilingual documents.
A complexity score Claude assigns, with high scores going to review.
The current rules, with more reviewers added.
Failed validation checks plus any fields the extractor marks as uncertain, regardless of document length.

questions.question: A customs extractor must assign a tariff code to each product. Some descriptions fit two codes with different duty rates, and the extractor picks one without saying so. Wrong codes lead to fines. Which two changes fit? (select two)

options.text: Have the extractor flag descriptions that fit more than one code, listing each candidate with its duty rate.
Have the extractor pick the best match and record a confidence score next to it.
Send each flagged tariff code to a customs specialist who decides before the declaration is filed.
Add a rules table of common products and codes and let the extractor handle the rest.

questions.question: A support agent runs one long session per chat channel, serving customers one after another. Last week it offered a pickup at the previous customer’s address to the next customer. How should the design change?

options.text: Start a new agent session for each case and load only that customer’s verified case facts.
Start a new session per case with a brief summary of the previous customer’s case.
Keep one session and compact it between customers.
Start a new session per case but reuse the previous case’s tool results.

questions.question: Policy says legal threats go to a human. A customer writes: “If my delivery date is wrong again, I will take you to small claims court. When will it arrive?” The agent could answer the date from lookup_order. Which two actions are correct? (select two)

options.text: Escalate under the legal-threat policy, even though the agent could answer the delivery question.
Answer the delivery question first and escalate only if the customer repeats the threat.
Include in the handoff the order details, the customer’s exact words and what the agent has already verified.
Include a summary of the customer’s tone in the handoff and leave out the exact wording.

questions.question: After six hours in one session, a research coordinator cites sources it rejected earlier, repeats questions subagents already answered and drifts from the report format, although its context window isn’t full. What should the team do?

options.text: Repeat the format rules and the list of rejected sources at the end of each new prompt.
Move to a model with a bigger context window and keep the session running.
Have the coordinator review its whole six-hour history and list its own mistakes.
Start a fresh session seeded with a concise summary of accepted findings, their sources and open questions.

questions.question: This week’s Key Findings lists a drop in teen smoking, replicated in three studies, next to a rise in vaping from one small online survey. Council members may read both as equally certain. How should the report change?

options.text: Keep both in Key Findings and add the survey’s sample size in brackets.
Separate findings into a well-established section and a contested section, each with its own evidence summary.
Keep both, listing the replicated finding first.
Move the vaping result to a methodology note.

questions.question: A state health data portal has returned errors all morning. The search subagent retried it 40 times this run, slowing the whole pipeline, and the draft says nothing about the missing state figures. The report is due at 9 a.m. What should the system do?

options.text: After three consecutive failures, stop calling the portal for the rest of the run and state in the report that this week’s state figures are unavailable.
Keep retrying with backoff until it responds, delaying the report if needed.
Use last week’s cached figures with a footnote and keep retrying in the background.
After three failures, stop and have synthesis estimate the state figures from county data.

questions.question: Two sources give the cost of a flu hospital stay: a national 2024 study in euros and a local 2026 study in dollars. The report shows both in dollars in one table, and readers must be able to check each figure against its source. How should the table present them?

options.text: Convert both to 2026 dollars and drop the original figures.
Convert both and note the exchange rate and source years in a footnote.
Convert both and describe the method once in an appendix.
Show each converted value next to its original amount in the source currency and year, with the exchange rate used.

questions.question: Engineers build a research system with Claude Code. In each new session, Claude spends the first 15 minutes exploring the repository to find the subagent definitions, prompts and citation checker. What helps most?

options.text: Paste the full repository file tree into CLAUDE.md.
Add a short map of key folders and entry points to each engineer’s ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md.
Add a short map of key folders and entry points to the project CLAUDE.md.
Create a skill that explores the repository and prints its structure at session start.

questions.question: A document subagent reads 400-page regulatory filings and returns prose summaries. When synthesis needs to quote a passage, it reopens the full filing and searches for it, filling its context. Which two output changes help most? (select two)

options.text: Return each finding with the document path and the page and paragraph range that supports it.
Return each finding with its page number only and let synthesis re-read that page.
Return each finding with the filing’s title and publication year.
